7a470981d1689e5b: PETALING JAYA, Sept 8 — Former law minister Datuk Zaid Ibrahim has urged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to ensure the federal government and Petronas’ interests are protected as Putrajaya continues negotiations with Sarawak over the state’s oil and gas rights.
His comments come ahead of a meeting on the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), which Anwar is expected to chair in Kota Kinabalu on Friday.
In a post on X, Zaid expressed concern that political considerations could influence the government’s handling of Sarawak’s demands, particularly over Petros’ role as the state’s sole gas aggregator.
He said Putrajaya should ensure that decisions involving the country’s oil and gas resources were made transparently and with the wider national interest in mind.
“Anwar must not exchange political support for oil and gas to Sarawak,” he said.
Zaid also questioned whether Petros’ position as Sarawak’s sole gas aggregator would be further strengthened following the meeting, claiming the role could be worth RM10 billion annually.
He pointed to Sarawak’s previous success in imposing its state sales tax on petroleum products, which he said had brought the state billions of ringgit in revenue.
Let the courts settle legal dispute, says Zaid
Zaid, who recently joined PAS, said disagreements over the respective legal rights of Sarawak and Petronas should ultimately be determined through the courts rather than political negotiations.
“Let the Federal Court decide; let the rights of Petronas be litigated,” he said.
The former minister said discussions surrounding MA63 should be conducted openly and should balance Sarawak’s constitutional rights with the interests of the federation as a whole.

He also called on opposition parties and Umno leaders to state their positions on the dispute, questioning whether political parties were reluctant to speak out because of the influence East Malaysian parties wield in determining who commands a parliamentary majority.
Sarawak and Petronas have been locked in negotiations over the state’s oil and gas regulatory framework and Petros’ role in the gas sector.
The dispute has raised broader questions over the relationship between federal petroleum laws, Sarawak’s state legislation and the rights arising from MA63.
d05005bb01188e83: The UK government has considered the evidence and concluded that it spends far too much time considering the evidence. In a letter sent to all ministers on Monday, Chancellor John Healey, First Secretary of State Louise Haigh, and Attorney General Ellie Reeves said "consultation culture" had become an "industry of dither and delay" and told departments that the default should be to make a decision and get on with it. The ministers argued that formal consultations too often fail to reach those with the most relevant perspectives and can drag policies towards a "lowest common denominator outcome." The proposed cure is fewer formal consultations. These should generally take place only when legally required, when not holding one would be "conspicuously unfair," or when ministers decide there is a good reason to seek outside input that way. Previous promises to consult aren't necessarily safe either. Departments have been told to consider each case afresh rather than assume that past consultations or commitments require another. The government also wants to start removing what it says are thousands of unnecessary consultation and reporting requirements from the statute book. Its starting position is that these requirements should be repealed and retained "only by exception," with departments asked to look for opportunities to bin them through legislation already in the works. This is separate from Whitehall's other effort to wean itself off consultants, although the timing invites comparison. The government promised in 2024 to tighten controls on consultancy spending and deliver annual savings of £1.2 billion by 2026. As The Register reported in July, that didn't stop the Home Office from awarding Deloitte and PA Consulting contracts worth up to £200 million and £150 million respectively for data and analytics services. The National Audit Office also warned last year that the Treasury lacked comprehensive data on consultancy spending, while Parliament's Public Accounts Committee said in March that departments weren't complying with Cabinet Office controls designed to rein it in. Consultations aren't consultancies, of course. One involves asking interested parties what they think before making policy; the other can involve paying them rather a lot of money for their advice. Whitehall appears keen to cut down on both. The new drive doesn't stop at consultation. Ministers are also being encouraged to accept a higher risk of legal challenge when pushing ahead with policy. The letter says that where there is a "tenable legal argument," ministers can choose to proceed even when government lawyers assess the legal risk as high. Guidance for government lawyers is due to be updated this week to make that explicit. Judicial review is getting attention too. The government wants to extend reforms limiting challenges to nationally significant infrastructure projects beyond energy schemes to transport, water, and other major developments. Having identified consultation, legal caution, and judicial review as obstacles, Whitehall will now begin the traditionally straightforward business of changing Whitehall. ®

a3fa6fe135c24c69: KUALA LUMPUR: All 72 registered political parties have been urged to submit their positions in writing on the proposed Political Financing Bill.

Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said official responses from each party would provide a clearer picture of whether they supported or opposed the Bill, or had alternative proposals.
She said the responses should be formally submitted and signed by the respective party secretaries-general, rather than relying on individual politicians' views or informal surveys.
"If we merely survey politicians, sometimes they say their views are not binding on their political parties.
"That is why I am proposing that we obtain official responses from the political parties.
"That way, we will have clearer evidence of which parties agree, disagree or have proposals for improvement," she said at a press conference after the 2026 Political Funding Convention here today.
Asked whether the Bill could be completed before the 16th General Election (GE16), Azalina said she did not know when the election would be held.
Earlier, in her speech, Azalina said the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) of the Prime Minister's Department had conducted 18 engagement sessions.

"This included 12 sessions at the state level involving 1,544 participants comprising representatives from political parties, government agencies, academics, civil society organisations, the business sector and youths," she said.
Azalina said the Madani government remained committed to implementing the reform.
She said BHEUU had taken over the study on drafting the Political Financing Bill in May 2023.
"The Cabinet, on Sept 8, 2023, agreed in principle to the proposal to draft the Bill," she said.

42d8c08d6e0720e1: PUTRAJAYA: Five per cent of Malaysian students have been victims of cyberbullying, exceeding the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) average of three per cent, according to the 2025 Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA).
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the issue requires serious attention because bullying no longer stops when a student leaves school grounds, but continues in the digital space.

"Schoolyard bullying may end when a child goes home, but cyberbullying follows them back."

b836660325a47711: KUALA LUMPUR: Veteran actor and comedian Sathiya, 62, is busy filming a Tamil telemovie scheduled for broadcast during the Deepavali celebrations.
His daughter Amani Nair Satya, 37, said that her father was in excellent health and increasingly active, accepting acting offers and effectively returning to work as usual.
"Dad is doing very well right now. He is quite busy filming a Tamil telemovie for the upcoming Deepavali celebration.

"However, his hospital treatment is ongoing. There is a waiting period involved as he needs to undergo specific exercises for his leg. Nevertheless, Dad is very happy to be able to work again," she told Harian Metro yesterday.
Amani added that, in addition to accepting offers for Malay dramas, her father acts in Tamil productions every year, particularly for Deepavali.
"Usually, Dad acts in Tamil productions. He receives offers every year, though last year he couldn't act because he had just undergone surgery.

"Even now, he isn't using a prosthetic leg, but he can manage on his own. Dad is truly brave; he does everything while seated in his wheelchair. He propels himself from his bed to the bathroom and can shower by himself.
"My mother, my siblings, and I are happy to see Dad so cheerful and healthy."
"When he is at home, Dad spends his entire rest time attending to his grandchildren's needs," she said.
When asked about the prosthetic leg, Amani mentioned that the doctor said the outer part of her father's leg looked good, but the internal tissue still required time to heal.

Amani explained that Sathiya is scheduled for a follow-up appointment with a specialist at Ampang Hospital this coming October for an X-ray, after which the doctor will decide whether he can use a prosthetic leg.
Sathiya has already completed filming for the animated movie Zan Orang Utan produced by KRU Studios.
On March 8, Sathiya was taken to Ampang Hospital after complaining of dizziness, experiencing yellowing eyes and vomiting while at home.
The Pi Mai Pi Mai Tang Tu actor subsequently underwent surgery on March 9 to amputate his left leg above the knee, following the doctor's diagnosis of an infection.
After receiving treatment at Ampang Hospital for a week, Sathiya was discharged on March 16 and is currently required to attend specialist check-ups according to his scheduled appointments.
652cb7e777cae8e7: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has proposed five key elements for the Political Funding Bill, including specific penalties for political parties involved in financial misconduct and irregularities.
MACC National Governance Planning Division deputy director Mohd Gunawan Che Ab Aziz said the core pillars were transparency, accountability, equality, independence and inclusiveness.
On transparency, Gunawan said political parties and candidates must fully disclose their funding sources, contribution amounts and overall campaign expenditure.
"This involves financial reports that are publicly accessible, leaving no room for secrecy in political funding decisions.
While this poses a challenge, benchmarking against countries that have implemented such measures proves it is achievable.

"This step will also assist politicians in managing party operations and political activities by providing a clear, legal framework, particularly concerning financing," he said during a panel session at the Political Funding Convention today.
On accountability, he said the proposed Act must hold every party answerable to its members, voters and regulatory bodies.
"Clear penalties must be established for breaching contribution limits or failing to report financial disclosures.
These must be enforced by responsible regulatory bodies, whether it is the MACC, the Election Commission (EC), or an independent entity."
Gunawan said contribution caps and conditional public funding were vital to ensuring political equality.
"This ensures that both minor and major political parties enjoy a fairer playing field."
He said statutory independence was critical for the regulatory authority, which must operate free from interference by the government or external entities.
"This regulatory body holds a massive trust to ensure the law is executed effectively.
"The final element, inclusiveness, requires opening the floor to all stakeholders, including civil society and political parties themselves.
"They must be involved in drafting a truly comprehensive law that does not stifle democracy."

0e5ec205f89a07a9: AFTER a five-hour wait for petrol, Mongolian pensioner Nasanjargal is still 10 places from the pump, with dozens of cars behind him in a queue snaking into the arid steppe.
"Fuel is unavailable, there are huge queues everywhere," he told AFP from his motionless Toyota sedan after a one-and-a-half hour drive from the capital Ulaanbaatar.
Sandwiched between Russia and China, landlocked Mongolia has historically imported more than 95 per cent of its petrol from its vast northern neighbour.

But Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil facilities have disrupted supplies in recent months, triggering a relentless fuel shortage that has depleted Mongolia's limited stockpiles and raised questions about its energy security.
The shortages have roiled logistics, lifted costs and ruined the plans of many Mongolians accustomed to taking advantage of the short summer season with a road trip in the picturesque countryside.
Nasanjargal, a former police officer who goes by one name, said he was "out of options."
"I headed out this way hoping things might be better out in the rural areas," he said, his young granddaughter shifting impatiently in the back seat.
"It's the same story everywhere."
The prolonged crisis has increased pressure on Mongolian authorities to ensure unfettered supply of fuel.
Government responses have included daily individual caps on fuel purchases, a ban on stockpiling and an alternating licence-plate scheme intended to reduce the number of cars filling up.
But the rationing has frustrated many ordinary citizens, with Nasanjargal telling AFP that the lines are "very troublesome and extremely difficult overall."
Beyond crowded Ulaanbaatar – notorious for its daily traffic – fuel shortages present other challenges for rural, tourism-dependent regions.
Munkhchuluun Samdannyam, the governor of central Dundgovi province, told AFP that his local government's "first priority" was the needs of tourists and herders.
"Under Gobi (Desert) conditions, herders do not draw water from wells by hand. They mostly use motors and pumps.
"And to operate those motors, gasoline is necessary," Munkhchuluun said on the sidelines of an international summit on desertification hosted by Mongolia last month.
"For everyone else, we are trying to manage and coordinate the situation as best we can," he said.

Mongolia's vast size and relatively small population of 3.6 million means that the government has limited resources for building the necessary infrastructure, Telmen Altanshagai, an independent policy analyst specialising in Mongolia's energy security, told AFP.
"As geopolitics shifted, the country started talks with Kazakhstan on the trade of petroleum products," Telmen said.
"More recently, the current crisis forced the government to import fuel from South Korea and China," she added.
But as diversification of imports becomes a political imperative, Telmen said, "it doesn't address the fundamental question of energy dependency" on foreign providers.
In a potential breakthrough for Mongolia's energy security, work is under way on the country's first domestic oil refinery, with operations targeted to begin in 2028.

Prime Minister Nyam-Osor Uchral, in office since March, has staked his reputation on his government's ability to manage the crisis, saying last month that he was "fully responsible for overseeing the oil industry."
Telmen told AFP that any long-term solution must involve electrification of transport.
But in bustling Ulaanbaatar, electric-vehicle charging infrastructure remains limited, let alone across the vast, sparsely populated steppe.
The country's logistics still rely heavily on diesel-powered trucks, leaving freight operators vulnerable to disruptions that have been increasingly acute this summer.
They have also raised costs for operators of logistics networks.
"When I came into the city yesterday, fuel was virtually impossible to find," said Enkhbayar Myanganbayar, a 25-year-old truck driver.
"Regarding diesel fuel prices, in just the past 15 days, prices jumped," he said.
"Previously, it cost around 4,000 to 4,200 tugrik (US$1.11-US$1.17, per litre), but now it's over 4,600 and pushing close to 4,700 tugrik."
The volatile supply situation has weighed on ordinary drivers, with prices and availability fluctuating at each petrol station across the country.
In one grassroots effort to ease headaches, an online platform has been created to allow users to upload real-time updates on availability, prices and waiting times.
But many pumps have simply closed up.
When AFP returned to the petrol station where Nasanjargal had been waiting two days later, it was only open to emergency vehicles.
* The writers are from AFP

3c60b9d6fc368d5b: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 8 — The Johor government has directed a large-scale operation to hunt and capture five feral dogs that attacked a two-year-old girl in Kampung Tambak in Batu Pahat last weekend.

Johor religious committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khaled said efforts are being carried out by the Batu Pahat district office in collaboration with the Veterinary Services Department (DVS) and police.
He said the operation will be intensified for at least a week with deployment of various methods to ensure the detection of the dogs and their eventual capture.
“The methods would use a host of techniques that include monitoring and surveillance operations that is permitted under the law.

“Our commitment is to overcome the feral and stray dog problem in the area to ensure that similar incidents do not happen to others,” he told reporters during a visiting Nur Haira Wafiqah Muhammad Hamizi who is currently receiving treatment at the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) of the Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) here today.
Last Saturday, Nur Haira was found covered in blood with head and facial injuries after being mauled by a group of five feral dogs.
She was later rushed to hospital for medical treatment to her injuries.
Mohd Fared said the immediate capture of the feral animals involved needs to be carried out to ensure that they are free of rabies.
He said this was important not only to ensure public safety, but to also reduce concerns on Nur Haira’s long-term health.
“So this requires immediate action so that the feral and stray dogs in the area can be checked and examined for rabies,” he said, adding that priority is to ensure the child’s recovery.
Mohd Fared, who is also the Semerah assemblyman, said the state government is fully committed to cover Nur Haira’s medical and rehabilitation costs as she is expected to undergo a lengthy recovery.
He also called on the relevant authorities to look into Nur Haira family’s mental trauma and psychological well-being.

Mohd Fared said that priority to the incident, the Batu Pahat Municipal Council (MPBP) together with DVS had carried out operations on August 12, 26 and 30 where they successfully captured 22 stray dogs in the area.
Despite this, he said the number of stray and feral dogs still roaming in the area showed that continuous efforts are needed.
992a91d5d1d7c50e: TEMERLOH: A father was stunned to discover that his 2-year-old daughter had allegedly been mistreated at a nursery in Mentakab whose caregivers were known to his family.
What made the incident even more distressing was that his wife was friends with the caregiver.
Muhammad Nurfaiz, 32, said his family only learnt about the incident after his aunt informed them that a video allegedly showing the incident involving his daughter had gone viral on social media.

"We were shocked and never expected her (the caregiver) to behave that way, as my wife was close to the individual involved. We could not believe it, as my family had known the nursery for a long time.
"My daughter has been attending the nursery for the past two years," he said.
Nurfaiz said there had been occasions when his daughter would cry or refuse to attend the nursery.
He said after realising that his daughter was the child seen in the viral video, his wife lodged a police report on Sept 5, hoping the authorities would take action.

Meanwhile, Pahang Social Welfare Department director Khairul Amri Ahmad said officers from the Temerloh office had visited the nursery yesterday (Sept 7) and submitted their findings to the department's headquarters.

Yesterday, Temerloh district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Nasyim Bahron said a 25-year-old female childcare worker was detained following a police report lodged by the victim's 29-year-old mother on Sept 5.
The suspect has been remanded for six days.
The case came to light after a recording related to the incident went viral on social media last week.
99cbe13eb6602d9e: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Malaysia Airlines is gradually resuming services to and from Jakarta, following the restart of operations at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport (CGK).

Passengers are advised to ensure that their contact details are up to date via the “My Booking” section on the Malaysia Airlines website to receive timely updates through email and short message service (SMS).

Customers may also contact Malaysia Airlines’ live chat support through its website or call its Global Contact Centre at 1-300-88-3000 within Malaysia or +603-7843 3000 from outside the country, said the airline. — Bernama
fdb220f4f0ffec41: PUTRAJAYA: Prestasi murid Malaysia dalam domain Sains dan bacaan meningkat dalam Program Pentaksiran Pelajar Antarabangsa (Pisa) 2025, namun pencapaian Matematik menunjukkan penurunan, kata Menteri Pendidikan Fadhlina Sidek.
Domain utama Sains meningkat tiga mata berbanding sebelum ini dengan skor 419 mata manakala bacaan naik 5 mata kepada 393 mata.
Matematik pula menurun 11 mata kepada 397 mata.

Fadhlina berkata peningkatan dalam Sains dan bacaan disifatkan perkembangan positif, terutama ketika purata negara Pertubuhan Kerjasama dan Pembangunan Ekonomi (OECD) bagi domain bacaan turut menunjukkan penurunan.
“Pencapaian Sains anak-anak Malaysia meningkat. Pencapaian bacaan juga meningkat, ketika purata OECD sendiri menunjukkan penurunan.
“Ini kemajuan yang harus kita hargai,” katanya pada sidang media mengenai keputusan Pisa 2025 di Kementerian Pendidikan (KPM).
Bagaimanapun, beliau berkata penurunan pencapaian Matematik perlu diberi perhatian lebih serius dan tidak boleh dilihat sekadar sebagai perubahan dalam satu pusingan pentaksiran.
“Pencapaian Matematik kita menurun dan penurunan ini bukan sesuatu yang kita boleh lihat sebagai perubahan dalam satu pusingan sahaja.
“Itu harus membuatkan kita melihat masalah ini dengan lebih serius, bukan dengan lebih defensif,” katanya.
Dalam domain Penyelesaian Masalah Komputasional pula, Fadhlina berkata Malaysia memperoleh 484 mata, sekali gus menjadi antara enam negara yang mencatatkan pencapaian melebihi jangkaan.

Beliau berkata dapatan Pisa 2025 turut menunjukkan murid Malaysia merasakan mereka menerima sokongan kuat daripada guru, yang disifatkannya sebagai perkembangan positif untuk terus diperkukuhkan dalam sistem pendidikan.
Namun, katanya, sokongan ibu bapa terhadap pembelajaran anak menunjukkan penurunan.
“Bagi saya, ini bukan soal mencari siapa yang harus dipersalahkan. Ini soal mendengar apa yang anak-anak perlukan daripada orang dewasa di sekeliling mereka,” katanya.
Fadhlina berkata KPM akan meneliti keputusan Pisa 2025 mengikut setiap domain terlebih dahulu, manakala kedudukan keseluruhan Malaysia akan diumumkan kemudian.

1704d59877fd1e74: KANGAR: A man and five teenagers were charged separately at the Sessions Court and magistrate's court here today with raping a 15-year-old girl in July.
Before Sessions Court judge Sharifah Norazlita Syed Salim Idid, an 18-year-old unemployed man was charged with raping the victim at a house in Simpang Empat here about 2am on July 18.
The accused was charged under Section 376(1) of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum 20-year jail term and whipping upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Mohd Alif Farhan Hassan prosecuted, while the accused was represented by lawyers Mohamad Alif Farhan Mohamad Supian and Zuhair Ahmad Zakuan.
The court allowed the accused bail of RM7,000 with one surety and ordered him to report to a nearby police station at the beginning of every month until the case is concluded.
He was also ordered not to interfere with the victim or prosecution witnesses.
The case was fixed for mention on Oct 9 for the submission of documents.
Meanwhile, at the magistrate's court, five male teenagers aged between 15 and 17 pleaded guilty after the charges were read before magistrate Ana Rozana Mohd Nor.
According to the charge sheets, the juveniles allegedly raped the same victim in a group in two separate incidents at the same location.
The first incident involved two of the accused between 3am and 4am on July 18, while the second involved four of the accused between 2am and 5am on July 19.
All five were charged under Section 375B of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum 30-year jail term upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Alia Suzila Chek Pi prosecuted, while all five teenagers were represented by lawyer Wan Nursyaheedah Wan Najmi.
The court allowed bail ranging from RM500 to RM1,000 for the accused.
The case was fixed for mention on Oct 7 for the submission of the teenagers' probation reports and presentation of the facts of the case before sentencing.
4e8146665f000be0: JERUSALEM: Israeli opposition leaders on Tuesday called prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu unfit to serve after a report that the UAE had warned him before the Oct 7, 2023 Hamas attack.

Haaretz newspaper, in a report excerpted from a forthcoming book by its reporters, said UAE president Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan spoke to Netanyahu a week and a half before the attack and told him that Hamas was planning a major operation.
Netanyahu's office called the report by the left-leaning newspaper "an absolute lie" and denied he spoke to the Emirati leader at that time.

Gadi Eisenkot, a former military commander who has emerged as Netanyahu's top rival in upcoming Oct 27 elections, accused the long-serving prime minister of evading responsibility for security lapses and resorting to "pathetic" excuses, such as saying he was not woken up soon enough on the morning of the attack.
"Netanyahu received dozens of warnings for Oct 7 and ignored them all. He is unfit," Eisenkot wrote on X.
Naftali Bennett, a former prime minister also running in elections, said Netanyahu "bears personal and direct responsibility" for the deaths on Oct 7, the deadliest attack in Israeli history.
"Netanyahu cannot continue to serve in his position for even one more minute," Bennett said.

Haaretz said that Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar, later killed by Israel, had warned a former Palestinian official that the militants were preparing "a terrifying operation" which he described as an "earthquake".
The former Palestinian official relayed the message to an Emirati advisor, who passed it on to the Emirati leader who then called Netanyahu, according to the newspaper.
The UAE normalised ties with Israel in 2020 as part of the US-brokered Abraham Accords under president Donald Trump's first administration.
Netanyahu sees close ties with the UAE as a key achievement.
The newspaper, quoting mostly anonymous sources, said that Netanyahu replied calmly to the warning.

5b3b223c4ef3d21e: CAMERON HIGHLANDS, Sept 8 — The implementation of the Parliamentary Service Act (PSA) provides Parliament with the scope to streamline its legislative role, including strengthening special select committees to assist the government in identifying shortcomings and addressing public issues, says Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul.

He said the enactment of the PSA created a new environment after Parliament operated under executive oversight for 33 years, enabling the legislative body to play a more independent role in contributing to national prosperity.

He said under the 10 ministry-related committees established, each is comprised of 12 Members of Parliament (MPs) representing both government and opposition backbenchers who do not hold ministerial or deputy ministerial posts.
“They have broad terms of reference and powers under the Standing Orders to summon any party for hearings on issues concerning the public or shortcomings in ministerial execution.

“These committees will produce reports and recommendations that can subsequently be debated in the Dewan Rakyat, ensuring their views and proposals receive serious attention from the executive,” he said.

He said this at a press conference following the opening of the Conference of Speakers of Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies 2026 by Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail here today.
Johari said this approach allowed any oversights or issues at the ministerial level to be identified early before escalating into larger problems.
He noted that previously, major decisions were predominantly made by the executive, and any operational flaws could lead to prolonged complications.

He added that the PSA also facilitated Parliament in planning and implementing reforms, as legislative-related decisions were now made by the Speaker and Parliament, with the minister in charge of law and parliamentary affairs acting as a coordinator.

Meanwhile, Johari said the conference served as a platform to share best practices between the Malaysian Parliament and state legislative assemblies to strengthen federal-state legislative ties based on the principles of federalism.
He said the conference provided an avenue to deliberate on enhancement proposals and produce resolutions to guide legislative institutions in the future.

Among the areas that could be strengthened, he said, was bringing the legislature closer to the public, including creating more opportunities for citizens and students to engage with Parliament and state assemblies. — Bernama

“This morning, two individuals broke into the Renoir Museum and stole four works of art,” said Bryan Masson, the far-right mayor of the town of Cagnes-sur-Mer.

“Spotted thanks to the town’s video surveillance cameras, the two individuals fled, abandoning one of the stolen paintings as they ran,” he said, adding his office estimated the value of the stolen works at €9 million (RM40 million).

Its collection includes objects and furniture that belonged to Renoir, including his easel and wheelchair, as well as portraits, landscapes, and nudes painted by the artist.
The mayor said it took just five minutes for the authorities to respond.
“The museum alarm went off at 5.48am. At 5.53am, just five minutes later, our municipal police were on the scene,” he said.

AGOS Asia said AI is now accelerating that evolution, but the challenge for organisations is moving beyond deploying new tools to redesigning the processes, roles and operating models needed to generate measurable business value.
These issues will take centre stage at the AGOS GBS Summit 2026, which returns for its ninth edition on Sept 10.

7e68766b09b37fe8: SEPTEMBER 8 — The catastrophic flooding in Nepal has demonstrated, once again, the devastating human and economic toll of climate change. Entire villages swept away, roads and bridges gone, harvests destroyed overnight. The immediate priority must be to save lives and support affected communities. But the devastation is also a warning for Malaysia: physical hazards can quickly morph into macroeconomic shocks, and no country in the region is immune.

No single disaster should be attributed casually to El Niño or climate change. This year, the World Meteorological Organization expects a strong El Niño to intensify from August through October, raising the likelihood of above-normal temperatures and shifting rainfall patterns. In Southeast Asia, El Niño often brings drier conditions and raises the risk of drought and haze, even as the northeast monsoon keeps exposing Malaysia’s east coast and low-lying river basins to severe flooding year after year.

For Malaysian policymakers, the imperative is to prepare for the economic chain reactions that extreme weather triggers. Droughts, floods, and heat waves damage crops and infrastructure; with concentrated food import sources and vulnerable logistics, lower production can mean shortages, higher prices, and weaker purchasing power for ordinary households. The government faces pressure to subsidize prices or arrange emergency imports, while Bank Negara confronts supply-driven inflation alongside softer demand. Then comes the fiscal aftershock: if roads, ports, irrigation systems, schools, and hospitals cannot be repaired in time, disruptions become a permanent drag on productive capacity, forcing the government to divert development spending or borrow at short notice. A financing gap can easily become a long-lasting slump, so Malaysia must limit physical damage while reducing economic downtime and containing financial stress.

The scale of the challenge is staggering. According to the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction, direct disaster losses averaged $180–200 billion annually worldwide between 2001 and 2020; counting indirect and cascading effects, the total annual cost exceeds $2.3 trillion. Malaysia’s own flood losses swing sharply from year to year: the December 2021–January 2022 floods, the worst in decades, caused an estimated RM6.1 billion in damage across 11 states, before easing to RM622 million in 2022 and RM755 million in 2023, then climbing again to RM933 million in 2024. Each spike is a reminder that the country’s exposure to flood risk is not shrinking; it is simply lying dormant between disasters.
An aerial view shows houses damaged and deluged in sludge in the aftermath of flash floods at Timure in Nepal’s Rasuwa district on September 3, 2026. — AFP pic

Malaysia does not need to wait for the next flood to start planning. Prearranged financing cannot cover the full costs of a major disaster, nor should insurance be expected to. Its value lies in providing reliable funding during the critical early stage of a crisis, when delays hurt most and when overstretched agencies have the least room to improvise.

The right approach is to layer risks: budget reserves and disaster funds, such as those managed by NADMA, can cover frequent, small losses; contingent credit lines suit medium-size shocks; insurance and capital-market instruments such as catastrophe bonds should be reserved for less frequent but fiscally severe events. Getting funds to affected communities quickly also requires effective social-protection systems and contingency plans that are already in place well before the water rises, not improvised after the fact.

This process turns uncertain post-disaster liabilities into risks that can be measured, priced, and managed in advance, so the government is less likely to raise taxes abruptly, slash investment, or resort to emergency borrowing when disaster strikes. The benefits extend beyond the government’s own balance sheet: it gives Malaysian businesses and financial markets greater clarity about post-disaster policy, while enabling quicker restoration of ports, roads, electricity, and communications, the arteries an economy needs to keep functioning.

The economics of climate change has reframed the role of disaster-risk finance. No longer merely a peripheral instrument that pays claims after an extreme weather event, it has become a policy lever that protects fiscal space and improves the medium-term outlook before a crisis occurs: a macroeconomic firewall for fiscal policy, financial stability, and infrastructure planning.

Nepal’s tragedy is a stark illustration of what happens when a country is caught unprepared. As a strengthening El Niño threatens the region this year, the task for Malaysia is clear: prevent natural disasters from becoming humanitarian, fiscal, and financial crises. With disaster-risk finance in place, Malaysia will be better placed to restart its economy, preserve fiscal space, and protect the households and businesses that bear the brunt when the rains come. That is what real resilience looks like in a warming world.
*Ahmad Nizam Che Kasim is from the AGILE Research Group, Faculty of Business & Communication, Universiti Malaysia Perlis.
** This is the personal opinion of the writers or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.
c4bb1e2435721de4: PARIS: Mistral announced Tuesday that it had raised €3 billion (US$3.5 billion) in what it described as the largest-ever European tech fundraising, valuing the French AI firm at over €21 billion.
The startup, which is considered Europe's leading AI model developer, said the funding round led by chip giant Samsung would accelerate its research and help it to expand internationally.
The company's notional valuation has nearly doubled since a funding round exactly a year ago.
While still an upstart compared to the AI giants OpenAI or Anthropic, Mistral says it is carving a niche by offering models that companies can run themselves with their own data.

"This round means we can move faster on R&D, products, infrastructure and keep giving organisations the ability to run AI at scale, on their own terms," Mistral's chief executive and co-founder Arthur Mensch said in a statement.
"Organisations want to industrialise AI inside systems that are already complex: their own data, their own tools, their own compliance constraints," Mensch said.
Mistral said it had secured the backing of advanced manufacturers in the sector - with Dutch firm ASML having led the previous funding round and Samsung Electronics this round.
Mistral has stepped up its spending on infrastructure this year, including its first data centre, to be built in France.
It signed a deal in July with Microsoft to provide AI computing capacity while offering Mistral models directly to the US tech giant's clients.
Chief financial officer Johan Bergqvist told AFP the latest funding round reflected its belief that size was not the sole requisite for companies looking to integrate AI capabilities.
He described Mistral as "more of a mix of Palantir and Anthropic when it comes to what we can offer", referring to the Claude chatbot maker and the US data analysis specialist.
"We've seen that we can develop other models more cost-efficiently than some of our peers out there.
"So our need for capital is not as vast as some of those competitors," Bergqvist said.
Mistral also appeals to companies wary of exposing their data to US-based hyperscalers, since the AI models and their results remain in-house.
That push for digital sovereignty led French authorities in June to scrap Palantir data systems for its intelligence services in favour of a domestic supplier.
Mistral models are also being used to roll out a French government tool for part of the civil service administration.
"We want to expand across Europe," where the company is strongest.
"But it's also the Middle East, Asia, North America. We see increasing demands in all these regions today," Bergqvist said.

83d70b24ab9e770d: The UK government has corralled £7.8 billion of cross-departmental spending into a new space strategy intended to boost growth and national security through to 2030. The package covers orbital collision warnings, low Earth orbit communications, military intelligence, launch capabilities, and space science. The strategy brings together activity across government, including the newly created Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST), the Ministry of Defence (MoD), the Department for Transport, UK Research and Innovation, and the Met Office. The government says the domestic space sector is worth £18.6 billion and supports more than 55,000 skilled jobs. In a prepared statement, BIST Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said space was becoming a new frontier of economic and military competition. "This plan will help keep Britain secure by strengthening our ability to launch satellites, detect threats and protect the services people rely on every day. At the same time, this plan will enable our excellent UK industry to seize the boundless opportunities of this new age in space, creating skilled jobs, driving growth and improving connectivity for all of us." The plans include work to strengthen space domain awareness – tracking and analyzing satellites, rockets, and debris in orbit – backed by £149 million for European Space Agency (ESA) space safety work, including the Vigil mission, and £85 million for the National Space Operations Centre. The funding is intended to improve warnings of potential satellite collisions, hostile activity, and solar storms, helping protect power, communications, and navigation services. The government has also allocated £880 million during this Parliament to space control and space-based intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance capabilities. The investment is intended to help track military activity on the ground, identify potential attacks on satellites, and protect British assets in orbit. The strategy also identifies £2.8 billion for satellite connectivity, including the Connectivity in Low Earth Orbit program and the military's SKYNET communications system. Funding of up to £160 million through March 2030 has already been announced for the UK Space Agency's Connectivity in Low Earth Orbit (C-LEO) program, helping British companies and researchers develop satellite communications technology. The strategy also puts £40 million towards technology for servicing, assembling, and manufacturing equipment in orbit. The government says this could support everything from repairing satellites and clearing debris to producing semiconductors and pharmaceuticals in space. Another £148 million is allocated to European rocket programs, while SaxaVord Spaceport in Shetland is set to receive £30 million, subject to due diligence. A further £163 million will go toward space science and exploration missions, including delivery of the UK-built Rosalind Franklin Mars rover. The package also includes £57 million to improve rail connectivity, £190 million for astronomy and space science research, and £9 million to strengthen space weather forecasting. The government also plans to adopt a single approach to buying and developing space technology, beginning with satellite communications, in an effort to steer more work towards British suppliers, accelerate delivery, and secure better value for taxpayers. In July, the government's projects authority sounded the alarm over progress on Skynet 6, the £8.35 billion program to upgrade the military's satellite communications. The National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority (NISTA) gave Skynet 6 a red rating, meaning "successful delivery of the project appears to be unachievable" in its current form. Confidence had fallen from last year's amber rating because department-wide recruitment and resourcing constraints had created workforce shortages, while "sub-par supplier performance continues to delay delivery of the first SKYNET 6 satellite," the report said. The new document formally replaces the UK's 2021 National Space Strategy, which a House of Lords report warned last year had failed to turn its ambitions into reality. "The UK space sector lacks the strategic direction necessary for success," it said. ®
10312401d4c3c755: Google’s newest AI weather forecasting model predicts wind speed at 100 metres above the ground, roughly the height of a modern wind turbine. It also forecasts cloud cover and how much sunlight reaches the surface, and it updates every hour. Energy traders, grid operators and wind and solar developers already pay other companies for that data. The introduction of WeatherNext 3 now puts Google in their market.

Google DeepMind and Google Research released the model on September 3. It produces a global forecast every hour at up to five-kilometre resolution for surface variables such as temperature and moisture. The previous version, WeatherNext 2, worked on a 25-kilometre grid and refreshed every six hours. Google says the new energy variables are meant to help grid operators and developers predict how much power their wind and solar assets will generate, then match that against demand.

The consumer side of the launch has had most of the attention. WeatherNext 3 now powers weather results in Google Search, the Gemini app, Google Maps and the Google Maps Platform Weather API. Behind it sits an enterprise layer that matters more commercially. The same forecast data can be queried in BigQuery and Earth Engine or downloaded in bulk from Google Cloud Storage, with no model setup required by the customer.
Why the energy sector is buying AI weather forecasting

Grid operators are running a system that has become harder to predict at both ends. On the generation side, renewables now account for most new capacity. S&P Global Market Intelligence’s US Grid Outlook 2026 projects solar and energy storage as the primary sources of new capacity this year, at 51.2GW and 25.7GW respectively out of more than 90GW of planned additions.
Solar and wind generate according to the weather rather than demand, so each gigawatt added makes a short-term forecast more accurate.

On the consumption side, the new load is coming from AI. S&P Global identifies the spread of data centres across North America as a primary driver of the recent surge in electricity demand, forcing utilities to revise their load forecasts upward. Deloitte’s 2026 Power and Utilities Industry Outlook projects peak demand growing by roughly 26% by 2035, with data centre demand alone potentially reaching 176GW, five times its 2024 level.

The cost of getting a forecast wrong is straightforward. If an operator underestimates how much wind power will arrive, it has to buy replacement electricity at short notice, usually from gas plants kept on expensive standby. If it overestimates, wind and solar farms end up being paid to switch off because the grid cannot absorb what they are producing. Both outcomes are expensive, and both are forecasting failures.
The market Google is entering

Selling weather forecasts to the energy sector is an established business. Vaisala, Solcast, DNV’s WindGEMINI and IBM’s HyperWatch all compete in it. So does Jua, a Swiss firm that claims its EPT-2 model beats Microsoft Aurora and DeepMind’s earlier GraphCast on accuracy while updating 24 times a day, against what it describes as a typical four updates a day among competitors.

Google’s advantage is reach. The same forecast appears as a table in BigQuery, a layer in Earth Engine, an API in Google Maps Platform and the default answer in Google Search. No specialist vendor has that spread, and the hourly refresh closes the update-frequency gap those vendors have used to differentiate themselves.

The incumbents have one technical argument left. Jua’s published position is that physics-based models such as ECMWF’s HRES still outperform purely data-driven AI models during record-breaking extreme weather, because physics models encode rules about how energy and mass move through the atmosphere, while AI models learn patterns from past data.

Jua sells a physics-constrained product, so the claim serves its own interests. It also describes the conditions grid operators worry about most, when a storm falls outside anything the model has seen in training.
What is new, and what is being oversold

The architectural claim behind WeatherNext 3 is that it learns from real observations instead of from simulations. Most AI weather models, WeatherNext 2 included, are trained on output from numerical weather prediction models, which are supercomputer-driven physics simulations that carry a six-hour data lag. That lag can introduce bias in fast-changing variables such as rain and surface temperature. WeatherNext 3 ingests live geostationary satellite imagery and trains directly on readings from individual weather stations.

The shift is real, though narrower than much of the coverage has suggested. Google’s own system diagram shows the model taking in one-hour satellite mosaics alongside traditional historical analysis. DeepMind senior research scientist Ilan Price told Bloomberg the gain comes from not waiting for the next analysis and using the most recent information available instead.
Reporting puts the remaining data lag at three to four hours, down from about seven. Dependence on numerical weather prediction has been reduced, not removed.

The accuracy figures need similar care. Google reports improvements of up to 60% against NASA’s IMERG satellite product, 30% against MRMS radar and 10% against rain gauge readings at early lead times, measured using a standard scoring method for probability forecasts. Those are three separate baselines, and the percentages do not add together. The widely repeated claim of 50% better precipitation forecasting applies specifically to forecasts a day or more ahead. Every figure carries an “up to” qualifier, which makes each one a best case rather than a typical result.

Google published no independent third-party validation alongside the launch. It points instead to live evaluations by Brightband, whose leaderboard it cites in claiming WeatherNext 3 is the most accurate global weather model to date. A utility considering a switch away from a paid specialist will care more about performance in its own service territory, on its own assets, than about a global leaderboard position.
Google’s own stake in the problem

Google is selling forecasting tools into a grid problem its own industry helped create. The data centre build-out driving the load growth utilities are struggling to serve is led by the hyperscalers, Google among them, and Google has signed multi-gigawatt renewable procurement agreements to supply its own facilities.

Accurate prediction of wind and solar output is directly useful to a company matching large volumes of clean energy against a load that is both growing and variable. That is commercial logic, and it goes some way to explaining why the energy variables shipped in this release.

Google has not published pricing for enterprise access to WeatherNext 3, or said whether the BigQuery and Earth Engine data carries standard Cloud query charges or a separate licence. Utilities weighing a move away from a paid specialist will want that figure before they weigh any accuracy claim.
2025, more than 65,000 employees in its Corporate and Investment Bank were actively using the platform, while more than 90% of its engineers were using AI coding assistants.
The bank also said AI-based transaction screening allowed it to review more than twice the previous transaction volume while reducing manual operator checks by half.

Bank of America is using a generative AI-enabled system called EricaAssist with more than 18,000 customer service employees. The tool summarises why a customer is calling, retrieves relevant information, and recommends possible next steps while keeping the employee responsible for the interaction.

Bank of America said in July 2026 that EricaAssist can deliver contextual guidance in under three seconds and has reduced average call times by nearly one minute. The bank plans to extend the system to additional servicing scenarios and business lines later in 2026.

b546bc2ac8561fbe: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — With rising traffic volumes and frequent incidents putting greater pressure on highway operators, a new smart traffic control centre covering three major Klang Valley highways was launched today to enhance road safety and enable faster responses through real-time monitoring.
The centre will oversee operations along the Sungai Besi Expressway (BESRAYA), New Pantai Expressway (NPE) and Kajang-Seremban Highway (LEKAS), all managed by IJM Corporation Berhad.

Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said past data showed that 85.4 per cent of traffic accidents on tolled expressways last year were attributed to human factors, while the remainder involved vehicle and environmental factors.

He said his ministry, together with the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM), was committed to further strengthening the development of smart expressways to provide users with a safer and more seamless journey experience.
“Based on data from the Malaysian Highway Road Accident Database System (MHROADS), a total of 26,675 traffic accidents were recorded on tolled expressways in 2025, including 839 fatality cases.

“With the increase in vehicles and growing user needs, our expressways need to evolve from physical infrastructure into smart mobility ecosystems that are safer, smarter and more efficient,” he said in his speech at the control centre’s officiating ceremony at the BESRAYA Loke Yew Toll Plaza here.

With more than six million vehicles using Peninsular Malaysia’s expressway network daily, Nanta said the federal government, through the Works Ministry, was committed to expediting the implementation of the Intelligent Transport System (ITS) under the Malaysia ITS Roadmap 2030.
Among the key elements of the roadmap is the adoption of smart mobility solutions that leverage real-time data analytics to optimise traffic management and user experience.

At present, LLM’s Traffic Management Centre conducts round-the-clock traffic surveillance through 873 integrated closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras and 278 variable message signs (VMS), enabling earlier incident detection and the timely dissemination of information to road users while expediting response efforts and traffic flow recovery.

Meanwhile, IJM’s AI-powered smart expressway traffic control centre integrates 144 CCTV cameras, 87 Video Incident Detection System units, 35 Automatic Number Plate Recognition units and 22 VMS units for the three aforementioned expressways.

Nanta said transforming existing expressways into smart highways was a collective responsibility involving the ministry, concessionaires, enforcement agencies, emergency responders and technology providers.
He then urged other highway concessionaires to adopt a similar approach in their traffic management operations to improve incident detection and enable a more effective and streamlined response.

“The use of technology does not necessarily mean replacing human labour; instead, it should serve as a catalyst for increased productivity and the creation of new employment opportunities requiring specialised skills.

“Our goal is clear in ensuring that the technology integrated can tangibly benefit the people, particularly in terms of safety, efficiency and overall journey experience,” he said, adding that IJM had assured him its latest move would not result in any displacement of its existing workforce.
Separately, a road safety programme using virtual reality (VR) technology was also launched to raise awareness among school students.

IJM Group chief executive and managing director Datuk Lee Chun Fai said the programme was part of a collaboration between LLM and the Royal Malaysia Police to promote safer motorcycle riding habits among students.
“The VR programme is targeted at school students, as 80 per cent of fatalities involve motorcyclists,” he said.
2c6d771dc2143dcf: GERIK: The familiy of the four climbers who were reported missing while participating in the Trans Gerah Expedition breathed a sigh of relief after they were all found safe, thus ending the family's wait which was supposed to last only five days and four nights but extended to 11 days.

Ahmad Ridhuan Abdullah, 44, brother-in-law of Wan Ahmad Aslam Wan Zairudin, 39, said the delay had caused the family's anxiety to escalate, especially after they had not heard from the group for several days.
"Our family was indeed very, very relieved. When we first found out they were safe and could be contacted, we felt very relieved, even though they had not been found at that time.
"Otherwise, we had not slept well for three days and three nights and sometimes had erratic food. So we are very, very grateful," he said when met at the Gerik district police headquarters today.
Ridhuan said the expedition was originally scheduled to last five days and four nights, but there was a delay after the group entered the route later than originally planned.
He said the family initially expected a delay of about a day, but began to worry when all six of them did not come out by Saturday and Sunday.

"They were supposed to exit after five days, but when Saturday and Sunday came, they still hadn't come out, the guide who was waiting for them at Pos Kemar began advising the family to file a police report," he said, who was also informed that the group's food supply was expected to face problems if they continued to stay in the forest, which added to the family's worries.

Meanwhile, Ridhuan said his nephew Ahmad Raef Wan Ahmad Aslam, 9, is not new to hiking as he has been involved in climbing activities since young but the family was still worried when the expedition to The Mount Trans Gerah lasted for 11 days.
He said his nephew had climbed several mountains including Mount Tahan and Mount Ledang, in addition to participating in the G7 climb.

He also expressed his appreciation to all agencies and parties involved in the search and rescue (SAR) operation, including the police, Fire and Rescue Department, Civil Defence Force (CDF), the Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan), the Forestry Department as well as mountain guides from Perak, Kelantan and the Orang Asli community.
Ridhuan said the six climbers were expected to be brought back to Shah Alam after all matters related to the police report were completed.

Previously, Wan Ahmad Aslam and his wife Siti Zulaiha Norizan, 39, as well as children Diya Raisha, 13, and Ahmad Raef, 9, as well as two mountain guides Shafiee Sidek, 49, and Hazman Mamat, 43, ere reported missing after climbing the mountain on Aug 29.
They were reported to have failed to exit the forest by the scheduled date on Sept 3 and the family members then filed a police report.
The family and two guides were found safe after search and rescue (SAR) teams spotted a smoke signal from the air in a remote forest area.
fdb0d1b2e95c8c88: AYER KEROH: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has remanded a senior medical officer for five days over alleged abuse of position involving the supply of knee implants worth about RM1.5 million.

2d70bdb8b959fc16: NEW YORK: Veteran actress Pamela Anderson has revealed she was given "around 10 years to live" following her hepatitis C diagnosis in the late 1990s.

Speaking at the amfAR Gala in Venice on Sunday (Sept 6), where she was honoured with the Award of Courage, the 59-year-old Baywatch star admitted that the terrifying prognosis altered the course of her life and clouded her decision-making, AsiaOne reported.
"It was a death sentence. That's what my doctor told me — that I probably had around 10 years to live," Anderson said.
"It was not a fear of death, but a fear of what might happen to my young children. I'm sure that corrupted my decisions. It turned my life inside out."
At the time, Anderson was consumed by anxiety over the future of her sons with ex-husband Tommy Lee — Brandon, now 30, and Dylan, now 28.
She also struggled with the heavy stigma attached to the illness.
"Just like the sexual abuse that I endured as a child, it felt like it was carved into my forehead: Damaged goods," she said, reflecting on the lingering "shame and guilt" of her diagnosis.
A medical breakthrough came in 2011 with the discovery of a cure for the viral infection.
By 2015, Anderson was declared free of the virus, though the recovery came at a steep financial cost.
"It took everything I had in the bank to pay for treatment," she said.
Now, Anderson has come to terms with her past, leveraging her personal trials to fuel a career resurgence and finding solace through her art.
"My truth has come through my work, finding ways to express myself through the arts," she said.
"I'm not a victim, I'm a victor. I am strong and capable, more now than I could ever dream of."
863553c7b6831364: PETALING JAYA: The Johor government has denied any link to the chairman of a housing committee at a federal statutory body who was arrested on Monday over suspected graft.

2892975103d2f101: JAKARTA, Sept 8 — Major airports in Indonesia reopened today days after a volcanic eruption had grounded flights, with authorities saying normal operations would resume gradually.
The disruption, caused by the eruption of Anak Krakatau, halted nearly 3,000 flights and stranded more than 340,000 passengers.
Five airports including the country’s main hub serving the capital Jakarta reopened after authorities cleared volcanic ash from critical infrastructure.
Transport Minister Dudy Purwagandhi told reporters it may take “a bit” longer for flight schedules to return to normal.

“We will be operating these aircraft, but before we do so, we want to ensure their airworthiness. So, it may take a bit of extra time,” he said of the nearly 180 jets currently at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport.
“We ask for a little patience from passengers and the public, as we will be carrying out inspections to ensure that these aircraft are fit to fly.”
Airport operator Angkasa Pura Indonesia said in a statement that volcanic ash had been cleared from the runway and other areas to ensure the facilities were safe for flights.
Three planes had already departed shortly after the airport reopened in the early morning, including two commercial flights to eastern Indonesia, the minister said.
At the airport, an Indonesian businessman, Heri, told AFP he was supposed to travel to Egypt yesterday, but that flight had been cancelled.
“I’m relieved” that the airport reopened, said Heri, who like many Indonesians only has one name.
“That’s why we rushed over here to make sure we could leave today,” the 52-year-old said, even though he still did not know when he would finally be able to fly.
“I was worried for a while. To go abroad, we must prepare everything well in advance... That’s what had us concerned, because we couldn’t do things in a hurry and everything was still unclear.”
Nozomi, a Japanese tourist who only gave one name, told AFP the airport closure left her confused because authorities had not provided clear information.
“I hope things stay like this, no delays, no closing airports. I hope everyone can go where they want to go,” said the 37-year-old homemaker who came to Indonesia for a family holiday.
Anak Krakatau, which had a major eruption on Saturday, sits in a strait between the islands of Java and Sumatra.
The volcano erupted at least three times this morning alone, according to the head of the national Geology Agency, Lana Saria.
Anak Krakatau — meaning Child of Krakatau — has been sporadically active since it emerged from the sea nearly a century ago in the caldera formed after the 1883 eruption of Mount Krakatau.
A 2018 tsunami triggered by the collapse of parts of Anak Krakatau killed more than 400 people and displaced thousands. — AFP
6cd1507a07f28a0a: KUALA LUMPUR: The Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) in Sarawak has been officially named the venue for the national-level Malaysia Day celebrations on Sept 16.

The decision to hold the main celebration indoors was made to provide a climate-controlled and safe environment for dignitaries and cultural troupes, in view of the current haze affecting parts of Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia.

Information Department (JAPEN) Cyber Media Division assistant director Yumna Baharuddin said Sarawak's selection as host aligns with the 2020 Cabinet decision to implement a rotational system between Sarawak, Sabah and Peninsular Malaysia.
"This rotational system ensures that every Malaysian, regardless of geographic location, shares directly in the spirit and historical resonance of Malaysia Day.

"Following Penang's hosting in 2025, bringing the celebrations back to Sarawak underscores the Federal Government's unwavering commitment to strengthening national integration across all regions," she said today.
Elaborating on the significance of the date, Yumna emphasised the distinct historical significance of the two national observances.

"While Aug 31 commemorates the independence of the Federation of Malaya in 1957, Sept 16 marks the 1963 historic unification of Malaya, Sabah, Sarawak and Singapore into a single sovereign federation," she said.
This year's celebration retains the theme "Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati" (Prosperity Enjoyed Together), paired with Sarawak's unity tagline "Segulai Sejalai" (Walking Hand-in-Hand).

The main ceremonial event at BCCK will feature an array of symbolic and cultural performances, including an inter-ethnic welcoming segment blending silat, hadra, gendang pampat and lion dance performances.
It will also include the signing of the Malaysia Proclamation Book by national and state leaders.
The historical volume was transported under the custody of the Sabah State Archives, pursuant to the Sabah State Records and Archives Enactment 2007.
Other highlights include the ceremonial cutting of pulut kuning and a tri-state artiste showcase featuring prominent performers Dayang Nurfaizah, Aizat Amdan and Stacy.
Japen and its partner agencies have also arranged a series of satellite events from Sept 10 to 16.

These include the Formation Corridor Exhibition at Plaza Merdeka, division-level pop-up exhibitions across 10 Sarawak divisions, as well as activities in Putrajaya, Selangor and Kuala Lumpur to ensure widespread public participation. — BERNAMA

df37b93d8cedaf69: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The risk of volcanic ash from Indonesia’s Anak Krakatau reaching Malaysia is currently low, although changes in wind direction and speed as well as possible further eruptions could affect its movement, MetMalaysia said today.

Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said current wind conditions and monitoring of the ash showed that the plume was mainly concentrated around the Sunda Strait and nearby areas of Indonesia, BuletinTV3 reported.
“MetMalaysia will continue to monitor the situation using satellite data and atmospheric analysis.

“Information from global Volcanic Ash Advisory Centres (VAACs) also allows any potential movement of the ash into Malaysian airspace to be identified and communicated to the public promptly,” he said.
Earlier, media reports said continued eruptions from Anak Krakatau since Friday had spread volcanic ash and prompted six airports to suspend flight operations.
The disruption also affected domestic and international flights, including routes linking Jakarta with Kuala Lumpur, Singapore, Hong Kong, Sydney, Seoul/Incheon, Doha and Amsterdam.
On the potential impact if the ash reaches Malaysia, Mohd Hisham said the biggest concern would be disruption to domestic and international flight operations.
He said volcanic eruptions were monitored by VAACs under the supervision of the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO).

“If the information received indicates a potential impact on Malaysian airspace, MetMalaysia will issue volcanic ash threat warnings or advisories to the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM), Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF), airline operators and airport operators,” he said.

Mohd Hisham also clarified that the reduced visibility currently experienced, particularly in Sarawak and parts of the western peninsula, was caused by transboundary haze and not volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau.
b7399b7d2cf80384: YouTube was the most frequently cited website in Google AI Overviews across a panel of vitamin and supplement searches, according to new research. The video platform appeared in 186 of 350 AI-generated answers, or 53.1%, making it the only website cited in more than half of the answers collected.

Searcherries followed 50 searches daily from August 30 to September 5, 2026. The questions came from Google Autocomplete and covered topics including hair growth, energy, sleep, anxiety and weight loss. Every search produced an AI Overview, the AI-generated summary that Google displays alongside its search results.

GoodRx was the second most frequently cited website, appearing in 48.3% of answers. Healthline followed at 28.6%, Cleveland Clinic at 28.0%, and the National Institutes of Health domain, nih.gov, at 25.1%. Websites were ranked by the number of answers citing them, with each website counted only once per answer.

YouTube’s presence extended across 44 of the 50 queries. It was particularly prominent in the group beginning with “vitamins for,” appearing in 78.6% of those answers. Across the full panel, YouTube appeared almost twice as often as Healthline.

The research also found that AI Overviews frequently cited pages outside the recorded organic results. Only 32.4% of cited pages appeared in the organic listings collected for the same search; 67.6% did not. Matching by website instead of exact page raised the overlap to 52.5%, showing that some AI citations pointed to a different page on a website already present in organic search.

Individual answers were less consistent than the overall leaderboard. For “supplements for weight loss,” nih.gov appeared every day and YouTube appeared on six of seven days, while other websites moved in and out. By contrast, “supplements to help with glp-1 side effects” returned the same cited pages throughout the week.

Searcherries monitored a fixed set of 50 Google Autocomplete queries once daily using US English desktop results configured for New York. The analysis covered 350 AI Overviews and 5,036 citation occurrences across 572 distinct pages and 218 websites. Organic overlap was calculated within each search, counting repeated citations to the same page once; the recorded organic lists contained seven to ten results.
f91fdf044e2eb0a8: PETALING JAYA: Ketua Menteri Pulau Pinang Chow Kon Yeow digesa membentangkan rang undang-undang (RUU) bagi memperuntukkan dana sama rata kepada semua kawasan DUN, kata Setiausaha Agung DAP Loke Siew Fook.

afb91257fc146a32: JOHOR BARU: Johor has ordered a major operation to track down and capture five stray dogs that mauled a two-year-old girl in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, Batu Pahat.

State Religious Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khaled said the dogs must be captured and tested for rabies, with the operation to be intensified for at least a week. The incident happened last Saturday.

"The hospital is also concerned about whether the dogs that attacked the child were carrying rabies.

Fared said the operation involved the Batu Pahat district office, Veterinary Services Department (DVS) and police.

"Our commitment is to resolve the stray dog problem in the area and prevent a similar incident from happening to others," he said.

a65bc463c45bd256: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia recorded encouraging improvements in the Science and Reading literacy domains under the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) 2025.
Results from the triennial PISA study showed Science literacy rose three points to 419, while Reading literacy increased five points to 393 compared with the PISA 2022 report.
However, the average score for Mathematics literacy declined by 11 points to 397.

​​​​Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said PISA 2025 offered encouraging developments and noted that Malaysia's Science and Reading literacy scores rose even as the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) average declined.
"At the same time, there is a finding we cannot and will not hide — our Mathematics performance has dropped," Fadhlina told a press conference today.
"This decline is not something we can view as a one-off fluctuation. It requires us to look at the problem more seriously, not defensively."
Fadhlina added that Malaysia was among six countries globally to perform above expectations in Computational Problem Solving, scoring 484 points against the OECD baseline of 500.
"Computational Problem Solving reflects students' ability to break down complex issues into smaller parts, identify patterns, select key information, and structure steps to solve them," she said.

Addressing the drop in Mathematics, Fadhlina said knowledge alone is insufficient if students cannot apply what they learn to new situations, adding that the challenge lies in translating capability into better mastery.
"That is why the Mathematics Education Transformation Plan (RTPM) we initiated focuses heavily on conceptual understanding, reasoning, and problem-solving," she said.
"We do not want Mathematics to become a race to find answers. We want it to train children to navigate their way to the answer."
Fadhlina also highlighted positive student-teacher dynamics, noting that PISA reported strong teacher support.

According to the report, 91 per cent of Malaysian students felt teachers helped their learning, 87 per cent said teachers taught until they understood, 86 per cent received extra help when needed, 83 per cent were given opportunities to express opinions, and 80 per cent felt teachers showed interest in their learning.
"I take this opportunity to congratulate our teachers, who remain unsung heroes. Thank you, teachers," Fadhlina said.
"Amid all the debates on curriculum, technology, and examinations, let us not forget that education is ultimately about a teacher igniting hope in a child."
PISA 2025 was conducted from April 22 to May 30 last year, involving 7,624 15-year-old students across 157 schools and educational institutions nationwide.
2fd2d620e02a4dd5: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Malaysia could experience extreme heat and dry weather from January to May next year, with temperatures in some areas potentially reaching 40°C as a very strong El Nino, or Super El Nino, is expected to develop towards the end of this year.

Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the likelihood of the phenomenon occurring was now approaching 100 per cent, based on climate model forecasts from international observation and research centres, according to a report published by Berita Harian.

He said past meteorological records showed that very strong El Nino episodes were often associated with higher temperatures, dry weather and a serious risk of haze, similar to conditions currently affecting the country.
“Experience from the Super El Nino episodes of 1997/1998 and 2015/2016 showed that the country’s daily maximum temperatures at the time were more extreme than during other periods.

“The country recorded its highest temperature of 40.1°C at the Chuping Meteorological Station in Perlis on April 9, 1998, and 39.3°C at the Batu Embun Meteorological Station in Jerantut, Pahang on April 10, 2016,” he said.
Mohd Hisham said there was about a 70 per cent probability that the intensity of the current El Nino would exceed the strength of any El Nino episode recorded since 1950.

“The situation could cause northern and inland areas of the peninsula, as well as inland Sabah and Sarawak, to record higher-than-usual temperatures and increase the risk of hot weather and heatwaves from the end of the North-east Monsoon in January until May 2027.

“Based on the latest projections, more meteorological stations in the northern peninsula could record temperatures of up to 40°C during the peak of the hot season between January and May 2027,” he said.
He warned that rising temperatures and prolonged hot weather could increase the risk of heatwaves and affect health, particularly among children, the elderly and those engaging in outdoor activities.
“Reduced rainfall and longer dry periods could put pressure on water resources, including catchment areas and dams, while also affecting agriculture and other industries sensitive to water shortages.
“Prolonged hot and dry conditions would also make vegetation more susceptible to fires, increasing the risk of forest and peatland fires as well as haze, both locally and across borders,” he said.
ef22087e481b1daa: KATHMANDU: Dozens of young people congregated at Nepal's burnt-out parliament building on Tuesday to mark the anniversary of deadly anti-corruption protests that toppled the former government.
The gathering in memory of those who died in the demonstrations came as the Himalayan nation continues to mourn the vast loss of life from devastating floods two weeks ago.

The rallies on September 8-9, 2025, were initially sparked by anger over a brief government ban on social media but were driven by deeper frustration over economic hardship, corruption and entrenched political practices.
The unrest caused the deaths of 76 people and the torching of the parliament building in the capital Kathmandu, as well as the prime minister's office and other government buildings.
It also led to the downfall of the administration of KP Sharma Oli, setting in motion a series of events that culminated with the election of youthful Prime Minister Balendra Shah in March.
"The loss of life was of course terrible. But the impact on politics was worth it, we have seen changes," said former protester Aastha Shrestha, 23, on the grounds of the ruined building.
"It feels like the (current) government values the sacrifice we made," she told AFP next to a stack of burnt vehicles.
Banners bearing photos of people killed in the protests were hung in the parliament grounds.
Shah said on X that he hoped the anniversary would "inspire us all to move forward towards building a fair, transparent, and opportunity-filled Nepal."
Sushila Karki, who led Nepal as interim prime minister after Oli's government was overthrown, paid tribute to "all the brave individuals who lost their lives."

"Let us all perform our duties honestly, responsibly, and vigilantly... so that a situation never arises again in which people are forced to take to the streets once more for good governance and change," she said in a social media post.
An inquiry commission set up to investigate the violence submitted its report in April and recommended further probes against several officials including Oli.
The majority of the victims – 51 people – were shot dead, many in the head or chest, according to the report.
But there has been little genuine accountability, said Anish Acharya, 19, who came with flowers to pay his respects.
"Why did we sacrifice our lives, what did we get? There is no hope that change will come. Oli was arrested the next day but what then? The culprits are out and walking free," he told AFP.
"The government has not valued our sacrifices and demands."
Shah's administration is facing its toughest challenge since taking power as it leads rescue and recovery efforts following cataclysmic glacial floods on the border with China.
The Aug 26 disaster killed at least 1,399 people in the two countries, including 1,356 in Nepal, according to official tolls.
A total of 5,500 people are still missing in Nepal and China.
