801cdfbd0669b185: SYDNEY, Sept 8 — Social media giants face US$78 million (RM315 million) fines if they fail to protect young users from harmful content, Australia’s prime minister said today as he unveiled draft laws reining in big tech.
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese released draft laws that would place a “duty of care” on the firms behind popular platforms such as Facebook, TikTok and Instagram.
Social media companies would be held responsible for protecting under-18s from pornography, online bullying, content that glorified crime, and content that encouraged eating disorders.
“We took action because the community said ‘enough is enough’,” Albanese told reporters.
“We would no longer let Australian kids be treated as commodities instead of children.”
Social media firms face mounting scrutiny over their use of allegedly addictive algorithms and stand accused of directing users to extreme content to keep them scrolling.
The draft laws build on Australia’s world-first social media ban for under-16s, which came into effect late last year.
Companies found to be flouting their “duty of care” could be fined up to A$109 million (RM315 million), Albanese said.
The legislation includes a requirement that platforms allow users to “opt out” of powerful algorithms that determine what comes up on social media feeds.
“This will give Australians greater choice over their platforms and what they see,” Albanese said.
It would require firms like Meta, which owns Facebook and Instagram, to give users the option of turning off algorithms that tailor recommendations to their personal taste.
Communications Minister Anika Wells said big tech was facing a “reckoning”.
“Their platforms and tools have infiltrated our daily lives in ways that we could never have imagined,” she told reporters on Tuesday.
“Some good, but some with terrible consequences.”
Data last month found that under-16s in Australia were increasing their use of social media apps such as Instagram and TikTok despite the ban.
The draft laws would be introduced to parliament later this year after consultation with social media companies, industry bodies and civil society groups. — AFP

66a9233f94b85935: SEPTEMBER 8 — For generations, the traditional idea of success was relatively straightforward: graduate from university, secure a stable job and build a career. For Generation Z, that formula is beginning to look increasingly outdated.

Born into a world of smartphones, social media, e-commerce and now artificial intelligence (AI), Gen Z is entering a labour market that is fundamentally different from the one their parents experienced.
Their challenge is therefore not simply to find a job. It is to understand how to create value — and, where possible, create opportunities for themselves and others.

This does not mean every young Malaysian should become an entrepreneur. Entrepreneurship is not a universal solution to unemployment, nor should young people be pressured into starting businesses simply because they cannot find conventional employment. Rather, what Gen Z needs is an entrepreneurial mindset — the ability to recognise opportunities, solve problems, take calculated risks and adapt when circumstances change.
A smartphone is not a business strategy
It is easy to assume that Gen Z has an advantage because they are digital natives.

They know how to use TikTok. They understand Instagram. They are comfortable with online shopping, digital payments and content creation. Many are also experimenting with AI tools.But being good at using technology does not automatically make someone an entrepreneur. A smartphone can be a shop, marketing channel, office and content studio. But it does not tell an entrepreneur what to sell, who will buy it, how much it should cost or whether the business can survive beyond its first viral moment. This distinction is increasingly important as social media transforms the way young Malaysians perceive entrepreneurship.

The rise of TikTok Shop, creator businesses, affiliate marketing and personal branding has lowered the barriers to entering the market. Recent discussions on Malaysian youth entrepreneurship have also highlighted how social media and digital technologies are changing the way young people approach business. But visibility is not the same as sustainability. A viral video may generate thousands of views. It may even generate sales. Yet a sustainable business requires something more: customers who return, healthy cash flow, sound pricing, effective operations and the ability to respond when trends change.
Financial literacy matters more than going viral

This is where financial literacy becomes critical. Young people may know how to promote a product but still struggle to calculate its actual profit. Revenue is not profit. Sales are not cash flow. And having thousands of followers does not mean having thousands of customers. Entrepreneurship education for Gen Z must therefore go beyond teaching students how to write a business plan. They need to understand pricing, costs, cash flow, savings, financing and financial risk. These may sound like basic concepts, but they can determine whether a promising business survives.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The goal should be to produce graduates who are not only job-ready, but also opportunity-ready. — Picture by Hari Anggara
Universities need to rethink entrepreneurship education

Universities also have an important role to play. Entrepreneurship education should not be confined to lectures, examinations and business-plan assignments. Students should be given opportunities to identify real problems, develop solutions, test products, speak to customers, build digital campaigns and experience the discomfort of discovering that an idea does not work.
Failure, when managed safely and constructively, can be one of the best entrepreneurship lessons.

The goal should be to produce graduates who are not only job-ready, but also opportunity-ready. An opportunity-ready graduate may become an entrepreneur. They may become an intrapreneur within an organisation. They may develop a digital business on the side. Or they may use entrepreneurial thinking to solve problems within their profession. The important point is that they are prepared to create value rather than simply wait for opportunities to arrive.
From seeing problems to seeing opportunities

Perhaps the most important skill for Gen Z is the ability to recognise opportunities. Everyday problems can become business opportunities. Long waiting times, inconvenient services, changing consumer preferences, ageing populations, sustainability concerns and the growing demand for digital services all represent potential areas for innovation.

The question is whether young people have been trained to notice them. This is where perceived opportunity becomes important. Entrepreneurship is not simply about having a good idea. It begins with recognising that a particular problem can potentially be transformed into a solution that people are willing to pay for or support.
AI will change the game but humans still matter.

AI is adding another dimension to this transformation. For Gen Z entrepreneurs, AI can help with market research, content creation, customer communication, data analysis and productivity. It can reduce the time and cost required to perform tasks that once required specialist expertise.

But AI should not be mistaken for an entrepreneurial strategy. If everyone has access to similar AI tools, the competitive advantage will increasingly depend on what humans do with them. Creativity, judgement, empathy, critical thinking and the ability to understand customers will remain essential.
The future entrepreneur may therefore not be the person who knows the most about technology, but the person who knows how to combine technology with human needs.
Not everyone needs to become an entrepreneur

There is also a danger in romanticising entrepreneurship. Social media often presents entrepreneurship as freedom, flexibility and financial success. What is less visible are the long hours, uncertainty, failed products, inconsistent income and financial risks.

Young people should not be told that salaried employment is inferior to entrepreneurship. A healthy economy needs both. What we should build is a generation that has choices. A graduate should be able to enter a profession, work for a company, pursue freelancing, build a side business or eventually establish a company — depending on their interests, capabilities and circumstances. The real objective is economic agency with having the knowledge, confidence and skills to make informed choices about one’s economic future.
From job seekers to opportunity creators
Malaysia’s approach to youth development must therefore move beyond asking how many young people have found jobs.

We should also ask: How many are capable of identifying opportunities? How many understand financial management? How many can use digital technologies productively? How many have the confidence to turn an idea into something that creates value? These are not merely entrepreneurship questions. They are questions about the future of work.

Gen Z does not need to be told that everyone must become an entrepreneur. They need to be equipped with the mindset to recognise an opportunity when they see one. Because in an economy shaped by technology, AI and rapidly changing consumer behaviour, the most valuable career skill may not be knowing where the next job is. It may be knowing how to create the next opportunity.

c4c15599042385bf: KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy prime minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has proposed a Malay Education Mobility Index to measure whether education improves the socioeconomic standing of the Malay community.
Zahid said the index should track a person's socioeconomic background, learning achievements, education pathways, employment, skills matching and income growth.
He said education should be assessed not only by qualifications obtained, but also by the knowledge and skills acquired and their impact on social mobility.

“In human capital theory, education is an investment. But that investment only truly becomes capital when it produces tangible capabilities and mobility,” he said in his speech at the 2026 Malay Education Convention at the Putra World Trade Centre here.

“Our measurement must move from schooling to learning, and from learning to mobility – not just how long someone spends in the system, but what they acquire, where that knowledge takes them and the extent to which education improves their social and economic mobility.”
Zahid, who is also Umno president, said the party's education and research secretariat, together with academic institutions, should develop an initial framework for the index.
He said the Malay education agenda should be driven by data, outcomes and evidence, rather than the number of programmes, allocations or participants.

For decades, he said, the focus had been on expanding access through schools and institutions such as Majlis Amanah Rakyat, Mara Junior Science Colleges and Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM), as well as scholarships and access to higher education.

“However, the challenge is no longer simply ensuring Malays have access to education, but ensuring they emerge with valuable knowledge and skills that can improve their socioeconomic standing and that of their families,” he said.

He said education must also translate into economic value, noting that 35.2% of tertiary-educated workers in the second quarter of this year were employed in jobs that did not match their skill levels.

Zahid said although the 13th Malaysia Plan aims to increase the proportion of graduates in jobs matching their qualifications from 69.4% to 70.1% by 2030, institutions with a major Bumiputera development mandate should set a higher target of at least 80%.

Earlier, the convention approved seven resolutions to be brought to the Cabinet, including proposals for a national education mobility database and index, targeted early education interventions and greater involvement by UiTM alumni.

135f572247435462: MARSEILLE: Two thieves broke into a museum dedicated to French impressionist painter Pierre-Auguste Renoir in southern France on Tuesday, stealing "four works of art", one of which they dropped as they fled, a mayor said.
"This morning, two individuals broke into the Renoir Museum and stole four works of art," said Bryan Masson, the far-right mayor of the town of Cagnes-sur-Mer.

"Spotted thanks to the town's video surveillance cameras, the two individuals fled, abandoning one of the stolen paintings as they ran," he said, adding that his office estimated the value of the stolen works at €9 million (US$10 million).
The Renoir Museum was opened in 1960 in the painter's last home before his death in 1919.
Its collection includes objects and furniture that belonged to Renoir, including his easel and wheelchair, as well as portraits, landscapes, and nudes painted by the artist.
The mayor said it took just five minutes for the authorities to respond.
"The museum alarm went off at 5.48am. At 5:53am, just five minutes later, our municipal police were on the scene," he said.
The theft comes less than a year after eight items valued at around €$100 million were stolen during a daylight robbery from the Louvre in Paris.

The four suspected Louvre robbers have been arrested, but the stolen items have still not been found despite extensive searches by French investigators in the Paris region and exchanges with police in Belgium, Italy and beyond.

ccfa75a101ee6d2d: PARIS: Thieves stole three paintings from the Renoir Museum on the French Riviera early on Tuesday, the local mayor said.

The museum was created in 1960 in the mansion of the impressionist painter Pierre-Auguste Renoir on a hill in Cagnes-sur-Mer, near Nice, where he died in 1919.

Art thieves in Europe are committing more violent robberies and specialist gangs have been replaced by ad hoc ​opportunists recruited through social media, pan-European police body Europol said last month.

fccf47848545394c: Arm's latest smartphone platform is optimized for running AI agents on mobile devices and introduces neural graphics that it claims can deliver desktop-class gaming within a smartphone's power constraints. Announced at the Arm Everywhere China event in Shanghai today, Compute Subsystem (CSS) for Mobile 2 succeeds last year's Lumex CSS and reflects Arm's embrace of AI as a strategy for future growth. Arm sees itself as central to this shift, arguing that AI workloads currently run largely in the cloud but will increasingly move to devices at the network edge. "When every interaction has to travel to a datacenter and back, there's implications for latency, connectivity, the cost of delivering those services at enormous scale, so this is where we're seeing it becoming more distributed, and I think few doubt now that basically everything you can push to the edge you will," says Arm's EVP of Edge AI, Chris Bergey. AI has evolved from background capabilities such as speech recognition and image processing into tools people actively engage with, including generative assistants, Bergey claims. Agentic AI goes further by interpreting objectives, coordinating applications and models, and executing sequences of actions. "So you have repeated inference, application logic, system orchestration, multiple workloads operating concurrently, and so that means you don't just need more CPU performance. You need multiple high-performance CPUs working in parallel to keep all those different workloads running," Bergey explains. With this in mind, the C2 CPU cluster features a new top-end C2-Ultra core that Arm claims delivers up to 15 percent higher single-thread performance than last year's C1-Ultra. The C2-Ultra cores have a larger execution engine to keep more instructions in flight, and Arm claims more accurate branch prediction and better fetch and target prediction to keep the instruction pipelines fed. Arm's chipmaker licensees can mix and match components to suit their requirements, as usual, but the firm touts a flagship cluster with two C2-Ultra cores, six efficiency-focused C2-Pro cores, and two SME2 units (Scalable Matrix Extensions), compared with one SME2 unit in last year's platform. Doubling the SME2 capability enables up to a 70 percent speedup on the latest small language models, according to Arm, while the cluster topology supports private caches on the individual CPUs plus a large shared L3 cache. All of this is tied together by the DSU, or the DynamIQ Shared Unit. Arm says the cluster has been optimized to reduce latency and keep concurrent agentic workloads responsive. CSS for Mobile 2 also introduces dedicated neural acceleration for graphics in the Mali G2-Ultra NX, which Arm calls its first AI-native Mali GPU. Arm previewed the neural technology last year, giving developers time to prepare for the hardware. The GPU introduces an all-new execution engine, neural accelerator hardware, and a third-generation ray tracing unit, built for full-scene lighting and shadows. The hardware supports Neural Super Sampling (NSS), which upscales game graphics from 540p to 1080p, and Neural Frame Rate Upscaling (NFRU), which generates intermediate frames to increase the frame rate. Using both techniques means the GPU renders one eighth of the pixels contained in the final sequence of displayed frames, with the neural hardware reconstructing the rest. Arm claims this makes desktop-class graphics possible within a 1 W power budget. "The G2-Ultra NX GPU is able to sustain a 30 frame per second gaming session on content with very rich and intricate ray traced scenery. And this is really enabled thanks to a 70 percent reduction in the overall ray tracing workload, which then translates to a 30 percent boost in performance," says GPU Product Manager Deyan Lazarov. Arm also demonstrated other games running at 60 frames per second. Like the CPU cores, Arm is offering Premium and Pro variants of the Mali G2 GPU, allowing its chipmaker customers to trade off performance against cost. To encourage uptake, Arm has published its neural graphics SDK and sample code on GitHub, with support for the cross-platform Vulkan graphics API. As with previous Arm smartphone platforms, chipmakers must now turn the designs into working silicon before smartphone vendors can bring devices to market, possibly as early as next year. ®
f7dc31c0201ba4c8: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Sabah’s claim for 40 per cent of its net revenue will be among the issues discussed at a Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) meeting to be chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim this Friday.
Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said Sabah would host the meeting, which would also discuss outstanding claims and issues under MA63, Sinar Harian reported.
He said this after a working visit to the Kunak Lipids Sdn Bhd Phytonutrient Extraction Plant in Kunak today.
Hajiji said the Sabah government was grateful to Anwar, as nine matters under MA63 had been resolved during his administration, including the devolution of certain powers to Sabah.
“Previously there were four matters, so a total of 13 (matters) have been resolved. However, there are still other matters, including the 40 per cent payment,” he said.
Hajiji said the federal government had agreed to Sabah’s claim for the 40 per cent payment, but several technical issues remained to be resolved.

“They have agreed but there are still some issues, perhaps technical issues, that have been raised. This is a normal process because there is an appeal process, but it does not affect the decision for us to receive the 40 per cent payment,” he said.
He said unresolved matters would be raised again for consideration at subsequent MA63 meetings or negotiations.

In a separate development, Hajiji welcomed progress on the Kunak Lipids Sdn Bhd Phytonutrient Extraction Plant, which is nearing completion and is expected to begin producing vitamin E before the end of the year.

“I am very pleased to hear the briefing from Sawit Kinabalu and the company working with Sawit Kinabalu that the plant built to produce vitamin E is almost completed and will produce vitamin E before the end of the year,” he said.
Hajiji said the project was believed to be the first of its kind in Malaysia and could help increase revenue for Sawit Kinabalu and its partner company.
9df44ce289aaebc7: PETALING JAYA: The likelihood of volcanic ash from Indonesia's Anak Krakatau reaching Malaysia is low, says the Malaysian meteorological department (MetMalaysia).
Its director-general Hisham Anip said this was based on analysis of current wind direction and speed, as well as monitoring of the volcanic ash movement, reported Berita Harian.

He said the ash is currently concentrated around the Sunda Strait and nearby areas in Indonesia, adding that the main threat should the ash reach Malaysia would be disruption to domestic and international flight operations.
“MetMalaysia will continue to monitor the situation using satellite data and atmospheric analysis.
“Information from global volcanic ash advisory centres will also alert us to any potential movement of the ash into Malaysian airspace and we will then inform the public,” he said.

Ongoing eruptions at Anak Krakatau since Friday prompted six Indonesian airports to suspend flight operations and affected routes linking Jakarta to Kuala Lumpur, Singapore, Hong Kong, Sydney, Seoul, Doha and Amsterdam.

Hisham said changes in wind direction and speed, as well as the possibility of further eruptions, could influence the movement of the ash, which are monitored by volcanic ash advisory centres under the supervision of the International Civil Aviation Organization.

“If the information received indicates a potential impact on Malaysian airspace, MetMalaysia will issue volcanic ash threat warnings or advisories to the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia, Royal Malaysian Air Force, airlines and airport operators,” he said.

Hisham also clarified that the reduced visibility currently being experienced, particularly in Sarawak and parts of western Peninsular Malaysia, was caused by transboundary haze and not volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau.
8fdb0a97cb57ef47: PARIS, Sept 8 — Mistral announced today that it had raised €3 billion (RM14.1 billion) in what it described as the largest-ever European tech fundraising, valuing the French AI firm at over €21 billion.
The startup, which is considered Europe’s leading AI model developer, said the funding round led by chip giant Samsung would accelerate its research and help it to expand internationally.
The company’s notional valuation has nearly doubled since a funding round exactly a year ago.
While still an upstart compared to the AI giants OpenAI or Anthropic, Mistral says it is carving a niche by offering models that companies can run themselves with their own data.

“This round means we can move faster on R&D, products, infrastructure and keep giving organisations the ability to run AI at scale, on their own terms,” Mistral’s chief executive and co-founder Arthur Mensch said in a statement.
“Organisations want to industrialise AI inside systems that are already complex: their own data, their own tools, their own compliance constraints.”
Mistral said it had secured the backing of advanced manufacturers in the sector — with Dutch firm ASML having led the previous funding round and Samsung Electronics this round.
Mistral has stepped up its spending on infrastructure this year, including its first data centre, to be built in France.
It signed a deal in July with Microsoft to provide AI computing capacity while offering Mistral models directly to the US tech giant’s clients.
Chief financial officer Johan Bergqvist told AFP the latest funding round reflected its belief that size was not the sole requisite for companies looking to integrate AI capabilities.
He described Mistral as “more of a mix of Palantir and Anthropic when it comes to what we can offer”, referring to the Claude chatbot maker and the US data analysis specialist.
“We’ve seen that we can develop other models more cost efficiently than some of our peers out there,” Bergqvist said.
“So our need for capital is not as vast as some of those competitors.”
Mistral also appeals to companies wary of exposing their data to US-based hyperscalers, since the AI models and their results remain in house.
That push for digital sovereignty led French authorities in June to scrap Palantir data systems for its intelligence services in favour of a domestic supplier.
Mistral models are also being used to roll out a French government tool for part of the civil service administration.
“We want to expand across Europe,” where the company is strongest, Bergqvist said, “but it’s also the Middle East, Asia, North America. We see increasing demands in all these regions today.” — AFP

98aadb2f8b3723e1: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — If Malaysia were to have a law regulating donations to political parties, should it protect donors from being pursued by anti-corruption investigators after donating money?

Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said today that this was among the technical issues that have to be studied before steps are taken to introduce a political financing law in Malaysia.

Azalina today listed nine parameters or areas of the proposed political financing law that are currently being fine-tuned, including who the law will cover; the supervisory body; the source and limits of donations; prohibition on foreign donations; traceable ways of receiving funds; reporting, auditing and disclosure; and offences and penalties.
At a press conference here, Azalina gave examples of issues that still have to be considered under the proposed law, including foreign donors.
Azalina said some countries, for example, prohibit foreigners from donating, while others have procedures requiring foreign donors to disclose their donations.

“Secondly, when you donate, will you be subjected to income tax deduction, or you must inform the source of your money? If everyone who donates have to inform the source of the money, maybe many will not want to donate,” she said at a press conference after the Political Financing Convention 2026.

Noting that some people might donate to all political parties as a form of “buying insurance”, Azalina said another issue to be considered was whether the law would allow donors to contribute to more than one political party.
She added that there was a possibility that no one would want to donate to political parties if such a law were introduced.
“And fourthly, do we want to make sure that when people donate, MACC won’t come and disturb, ‘why you donate?’” she said.

Later, when speaking on the same point, Azalina said she personally felt that political parties could issue receipts to donors, but said it had to be studied whether “to give protection to donors”, as donors might be deterred from donating if they were pursued after making donations.
“But we must give protection to donors also. If not, who will want to donate right?” she said at another point.

“But I agree if it’s a foreign donor, we must have a certain process. There must be a procedure, whether select committee or Parliament is informed, because if a foreign donor wants to influence our decision, this is also a problem right,” she said.
Azalina had explained that the Prime Minister’s Department’s Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) had been carrying out engagement studies and surveys over the past two years.
Azalina today urged BHEUU to obtain written official views from political parties on whether they agreed with having a political financing law in Malaysia.
After that, Azalina said the proposed law would be brought to the Cabinet for evaluation from multiple perspectives.
She told the media that the Cabinet would then decide on the final “format” of the technical aspects of the proposed law before the Bill is brought to Parliament to be voted on.

Earlier, when speaking as minister in a speech at the same convention, Azalina said the government’s goal was not just to enact laws, but to ensure they were truly effective and capable of being implemented.
She had spoken of the simple principle of being “transparent but practical, stern but fair, and accountability without curbing the legitimate democratic process”.

Today, Azalina, when giving her personal opinion as a lawyer and MP, said politicians could easily find themselves being charged with corruption if there is no political funding law in Malaysia to regulate donations to them.

cdd1d447e1591e57: BEIJING, Sept 8 — Landslides in eastern China have killed six people with nine others still missing, state media said today, days after heavy rains unleashed by Typhoon Saudel.
A mudslide which hit Mingkeng village in Jiangxi province on Saturday left five dead and seven missing, state news agency Xinhua said, citing local officials.
Another person was found dead and two others still missing after landslides hit the nearby townships of Zuo’an and Tanghu.
The landslides followed days of torrential rains brought by Saudel, which first made landfall on China’s eastern coast at the end of last month.
Several cities suspended work, schools and transport services in the face of the heavy rains.
The landslide in Mingkeng damaged homes and destabilised roads, according to Xinhua. More than 170 rescuers were deployed to the site to scour for those missing.
The landslides follow devastating glacial floods in the Himalayas last month that have killed 43 people in Tibet, according to state media, as well as nearly 1,300 people across the border in Nepal.
There are more than 5,000 missing in Nepal and another 519 on the Tibetan side of the border.
Scientists say climate change is accelerating glacial melting worldwide and making extreme storms more frequent worldwide, increasing the risk of such disasters. — AFP

39063c565e71d954: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The New Economic Policy (NEP) fostered a culture of dependency among Malays and became too focused on ownership and government assistance, former CIMB Group chairman Tan Sri Nazir Razak and former deputy prime minister Tun Musa Hitam said today.

Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported that the two made the remarks at a forum titled “Remembering Tun Abdul Razak: Architect of Malaysia’s Development and Nation Building”, which discussed whether the NEP should be reviewed, replaced or remodelled.
Nazir said the NEP was intended to run for only 20 years and cited former deputy prime minister Tun Dr Ismail Abdul Rahman’s description of it as a 20-year “handicap”.

“We will be in serious trouble if we have to continue. And when it goes on for too long, this ‘tongkat culture’ becomes deeply embedded,” said Nazir, the son of second prime minister Tun Abdul Razak Hussein.
He said the policy should be reviewed, with greater emphasis placed on education and professional development instead of the distribution of shares and ownership.
“The NEP focused too much on the distribution of shares and ownership. And when you go down that path, all these ‘Ali Babas’ come up,” he said, referring to a culture of rent-seeking.
“I think we focused on the wrong theme in the execution of the NEP,” he added.
Nazir also questioned the practice of awarding contracts to Bumiputera businesses, particularly why politicians were allowed to choose the recipients.
“They (politicians) don’t want competition among Bumiputeras,” he said, adding that the lack of competition had weakened Bumiputera businesses.
Musa, who served as deputy prime minister from 1981 to 1986, said the policy had also made Malays overly reliant on government assistance.
“To me, the economic policy for the Malays has caused the Malays to become too pampered. Pampered by the government,” he said.
Musa said the NEP had benefited Malays and the country as a whole, but had also created a sense of insecurity, with recipients continuing to feel that government assistance was insufficient.
“People fear receiving nothing, but even when they receive assistance, they say it is not enough and ask for more.”
83b654983fc805ec: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — When Puan Suzana was diagnosed with breast cancer, she expected chemotherapy to be the toughest part of her journey.
She never imagined one of her greatest daily battles would simply be: eating.
"Some days, after going through chemotherapy, I didn't feel like eating at all. Even swallowing became difficult," she recalled.

As treatment progressed, Puan Suzana’s appetite dwindled and her weight began to fall. Every meal became a negotiation between what her body needed and what it could tolerate. When her dietitian introduced Valens Onthera+, a specialised immunonutrition formula, she saw it as a supportive part of her cancer care journey.
"I call it (Valens Onthera+) my “Susu Coklat” and I take it on days I find it difficult to eat or swallow," she said with a smile.

"On days especially after treatment, when I feel extremely weak and tired, taking “Susu Coklat” helps me feel a little stronger. My dietitian said it’s good for me as part of my diet because it provides the nutrition my body needs. I do feel a little more energised when I have it, especially after treatment.”
Puan Suzana’s story is one shared by countless cancer patients across Malaysia.
The hidden burden beyond cancer treatment
While public conversations around cancer often centre on diagnosis, surgery and treatment, an equally significant challenge frequently remains invisible: the struggle to maintain optimal nutrition.

Studies estimate that between 40 per cent and 80 per cent of cancer patients experience malnutrition during their treatment journey, making it one of the most common yet overlooked complications of cancer care (1, 2, 3). Yet despite its prevalence, nutrition often receives far less attention than other aspects of cancer care, even though poor nutritional status may affect patients' strength, recovery and overall quality of life.

Today, this often-overlooked challenge is receiving renewed attention in Malaysia following the publication of a pioneering local clinical study on the use of immunonutrition as nutritional support in cancer care.
New Malaysian evidence on perioperative immunonutrition for cancer

Backed by a growing body of clinical evidence, immunonutrition is recommended in international clinical nutrition guidelines for selected patients undergoing major surgery, particularly within Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) programmes (4,5,6).

Contributing to this growing evidence base is a Malaysian clinical study published in peer-reviewed journal Supportive Care in Cancer. This open-label randomised controlled trial enrolled 110 gynaecological cancer patients undergoing surgery at Institut Kanser Negara within an ERAS programme, which measures comparison of perioperative immunonutrition intervention against standard nutritional care.

The study found that cancer patients receiving immunonutrition experienced significantly better clinical outcomes than those receiving standard nutritional care. These included shorter hospital stays, faster recovery of gastrointestinal function, improved wound healing, better preservation of nutritional and functional status, healthier inflammatory profiles, and notably, zero hospital readmissions within 30 days after surgery (7).
The immunonutrition intervention evaluated in the study was Valens Onthera+, a Malaysian-developed specialised immunonutrition formula.

Beyond validating clinical benefits, the study contributes robust Malaysian clinical evidence to highlight the role and importance of perioperative immunonutrition in cancer care, beyond data drawn largely from Western and East Asian populations.
Bridging the gap to evidence-based immunonutrition
While growing clinical evidence continues to reinforce the importance of nutrition in cancer care, many cancer patients in Malaysia still struggle to acquire the much-needed nutritional support.

To help bridge this gap, the Valens Onthera+ “1,000 Cans of Hope” initiative was launched at the Psychosocial Support Summit that was held in conjunction with National Cancer Congress Malaysia 2026. It builds on the VALENS® Support Fund, a cancer CSR programme jointly established by Pharm-D Health Science Berhad (Pharm-D HS) and the National Cancer Society Malaysia (NCSM) which was officially launched on World Cancer Day 2026 in the presence of Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad.

Under this initiative, 1,000 cans of Valens Onthera+ immunonutrition formula are provided to eligible cancer patients identified through NCSM via comprehensive nutritional assessments and consultation by NCSM's clinical dietitians to determine individual nutritional needs and clinical suitability.
Making nutrition an integral part of cancer care

Speaking at the launch, Wong Chin Cheang, Group Managing Director of Pharm-D Health Science Berhad, said the initiative represents a broader mission to establish nutrition as a core pillar of cancer care.

"When people hear the word “cancer”, they naturally think about chemotherapy, surgery and medicines. Yet, one of the hardest parts of treatment many patients face is simply finding the strength to eat. Nutrition is far more than an afterthought; it is an essential component of supportive cancer care."
He continued:

"When we launched the VALENS® Support Fund on World Cancer Day earlier this year, we envisioned it more than a financial assistance programme. We want to spark a broader movement that recognises specialised nutrition as an integral part of comprehensive cancer care. The Valens Onthera+ “1,000 Cans of Hope” initiative turns that vision into action, in ensuring patients receive not only nutritional support, but also professional guidance from qualified dietitians who understand their unique nutritional needs throughout treatment."

Kol. Bersekutu (PA) Assoc Prof Dr Murallitharan Munisamy, Managing Director of NCSM, added that nutritional challenges are among some of the most distressing, yet least visible aspects of the cancer journey.

"Cancer affects much more than the disease itself. Patients may struggle with eating, maintaining weight and preserving their strength while navigating the emotional and financial realities of treatment. By integrating professional nutritional assessment with accessibility to specialised immunonutrition, we hope to help patients focus on what matters most: their recovery and quality of life."
“1,000 Cans of Hope” as a start of a broader movement

While the initiative provides specialised immunonutrition to eligible patients, Pharm-DHS and NCSM believe its significance lies in encouraging a shift in how cancer care is understood in Malaysia, and to initiate a broader movement towards a more holistic cancer care.

Built on this shared vision, the VALENS® Support Fund extends beyond nutritional support through patient and caregiver education, community outreach initiatives and nutritional awareness programmes designed to empower patients and families throughout every stage of the cancer journey. The Valens Onthera+ “1,000 Cans of Hope” is one such initiative to reflect this commitment.
For cancer patient Puan Suzana, the support she received represented far more than a nutritional formula.

“It reminded me that being strong isn't just about getting through treatment, but also about taking care of myself. Beyond giving me the help I need, this support brings hope and a constant reminder to never give up.”

8cd6d758a10bf6d0: NEW YORK, Sept 8 — Top seed Alexander Zverev romped into the quarter-finals of the US Open yesterday with a straight sets defeat of Italy’s Luciano Darderi.
Zverev, who had been taken to five sets in his opening two matches of the tournament, raced past 21st seed Darderi 6-2, 6-2, 7-6 (7/3) in 2hr 30 minutes on the Arthur Ashe Stadium court.
The brisk victory came as a welcome change for Zverev, whose marathon first and second round matches had finished in the early hours of the morning.
“I don’t know what to do with myself because it’s before midnight,” Zverev quipped afterwards. “I might go back to the practice court, I might go to a bar — that was a joke, unfortunately.
“Compared to the first two matches, the level has been going up.”
The 29-year-old French Open champion was in complete control throughout, punishing Darderi’s woeful service game to grab an early double break in the first set for a 3-0 lead.
Darderi, who has failed to go further than the fourth round at any Grand Slam in his career, never looked like forcing his way back into the set thereafter.
Zverev mopped up the first set easily and was soon back on the attack in the second, once again securing a quick double-break for a 3-0 lead before holding with ease to go two sets up.
Darderi did manage to rally in the third set, suddenly finding his range with some blistering forehands and holding off four break points in the 11th game to help set up a tie-break.

But Zverev’s superior service game meant there was only going to be one winner in the tie-break, a thunderous serve giving him a 5-2 lead before a scorching forehand into the corner took him to match point.
Zverev then wrapped up victory with his 13th ace of the match.
“I thought my level was very consistent,” Zverev said.

“It was just he started playing incredibly well in the third set. I barely saw anyone hit the ball as hard consistently as he did in the third set,” added the German, who will now face Dutch veteran Botic van de Zandschulp in the quarter-finals. — AFP
9ed2a3d4d3fcb9a4: PETALING JAYA: Penang chief minister Chow Kon Yeow has been urged to table a bill stipulating equal allocations for constituencies in the state, DAP secretary-general Loke Siew Fook said.
Loke said a Constituency Development Fund (CDF) law would ensure fair, equal treatment for assemblymen in Penang, regardless of political affiliation.
"This move is to ensure that equal allocation of constituency development funds can be guaranteed by law," he said in a statement.
Loke said the party’s central executive committee (CEC) believed the same principle should be extended to the federal level and implemented by all state governments across the country.
"CDF should be given equally, regardless of the political background of the elected representatives."
Last month, Chow said he would wait for a decision by DAP's leadership on enacting a law guaranteeing equal CDF following a call by a civil society group.

Currently, the Penang government sets aside an annual allocation of RM60,000 for each opposition assemblyman in the state, while government assemblymen receive an annual constituency allocation of RM500,000.

Loke went on to say that the CEC also decided that bills on capping the prime minister's term and the separation of powers between the attorney-general and the public prosecutor should be tabled and decided in Parliament during the October sitting.
Additionally, the CEC discussed preparations for both the Melaka and Sarawak elections.
"DAP will make the necessary preparations to defend currently held seats, as well as identify other potential seats to contest."
829d63d44a5c3b48: Storage vendors have been calling things “unified” for years. Sometimes that means one architecture. Sometimes it means several products sharing a management screen and a marketing budget. The term has accumulated enough baggage that a little skepticism is warranted. HPE Alletra Storage MP B10000 Release 6, announced in May, is now generally available. It brings block and file onto the same disaggregated scale-out architecture and OS code base, with independent scaling of performance and capacity and native ransomware detection across both. That’s important because enterprise storage is becoming less of an array decision and more of an architectural one. HPE was recently named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Enterprise Storage Platforms, which provides useful context, but a quadrant is still a snapshot. GA code is where the architecture has to prove itself. Unified, but not universal The B10000 is not intended to become the answer for every file workload in the data center. Massive-scale, performance-oriented unstructured workloads such as AI, analytics, EDA and media remain better suited to HPE Alletra Storage MP X10000. The aim with the B10000 is narrower and, arguably, more useful: consolidating block and adjacent file workloads onto a common architecture without forcing customers to scale controllers and capacity together. That distinction matters. Vendors have offered “unified” storage before, but the harder question is what is actually shared underneath: protocols, scaling model, software stack and operational experience, or simply the management layer. The architecture is the product The B10000 separates compute from capacity with a “shared-everything” architecture, allowing each to scale independently rather than requiring customers to buy fixed controller-and-media increments. Release 6 extends that model across block and file while retaining a common operating environment and management plane. The interesting part is therefore not simply the addition of file protocols. It is whether customers can consolidate block and the file workloads that naturally sit alongside them without recreating the infrastructure silos they were trying to remove. Disaggregation also changes the economics. If performance and capacity requirements grow at different rates, the infrastructure can follow those curves separately rather than making one drive the other. AI moves closer to operations Release 6 also extends HPE’s AI-driven operations model. Within HPE Data Services Cloud Console, autonomous health assessments can evaluate areas such as capacity and performance, while Storage Copilot provides natural-language interaction, recommendations and the ability to take actions. Agentic Support Automation pushes that model further. Unlike legacy support approaches that depend on known issue signatures, predefined rules or thresholds, it is signature-less: AI agents continuously analyze operational behavior to detect emerging anomalies, investigate likely causes and help drive remediation—even when the specific issue has not been seen before. Capacity exhaustion is a useful example. Total system capacity can appear stable and generate no alert while a single service begins consuming capacity at an unusual rate. Traditional monitoring may not react until a threshold is crossed; agentic support automation can recognize the behavioral shift earlier, connect it to the underlying operating condition and help initiate corrective action before the change becomes a disruption. That is probably the more useful test of the increasingly fashionable word “agentic.” The question is not whether AI appears in the interface, but whether the software can move from describing an infrastructure problem toward helping resolve it. Cyber resilience becomes layered Ransomware defense follows much the same architectural logic. The B10000 now provides native real-time detection across block and file, while Zerto adds protection at the application layer and StoreOnce provides integrated data protection and recovery. No single feature solves ransomware. The more interesting model is multiple detection and recovery mechanisms operating at different points in the stack. Storage competition moves beyond the array None of this means the array is dead. Someone still has to store the bits. But the competitive unit is getting larger. Controllers, media and IOPS still matter. Increasingly, so do the operating model, cyber-resilience architecture, scaling economics and the ability to support multiple data types without multiplying infrastructure silos. The term “unified storage” has been stretched pretty far over the years. What matters now is whether the unification extends below the management layer and into the architecture itself. For more information, visit HPE Alletra Storage MP B10000 web page. Contributed by HPE
bedc7e80e3ddc91a: KATHMANDU: Dozens of young people congregated at Nepal's burnt-out parliament building on Tuesday to mark the anniversary of deadly anti-corruption protests that toppled the former government.
The gathering in memory of those who died in the demonstrations came as the Himalayan nation continues to mourn the vast loss of life from devastating floods two weeks ago.

The rallies on Sept 8-9, 2025, were initially sparked by anger over a brief government ban on social media but were driven by deeper frustration over economic hardship, corruption and entrenched political practices.
The unrest caused the deaths of 76 people and the torching of the parliament building in the capital Kathmandu, as well as the prime minister's office and other government buildings.
It also led to the downfall of the administration of KP Sharma Oli, setting in motion a series of events that culminated with the election of youthful prime minister Balendra Shah in March.
"The loss of life was of course terrible. But the impact on politics was worth it, we have seen changes," said former protester Aastha Shrestha, 23, on the grounds of the ruined building.
"It feels like the (current) government values the sacrifice we made," she told AFP next to a stack of burnt vehicles.
Banners bearing photos of people killed in the protests were hung in the parliament grounds.
Shah said on X that he hoped the anniversary would "inspire us all to move forward towards building a fair, transparent, and opportunity-filled Nepal".
Sushila Karki, who led Nepal as interim prime minister after Oli's government was overthrown, paid tribute to "all the brave individuals who lost their lives".

"Let us all perform our duties honestly, responsibly, and vigilantly... so that a situation never arises again in which people are forced to take to the streets once more for good governance and change," she said in a social media post.
An inquiry commission set up to investigate the violence submitted its report in April and recommended further probes against several officials including Oli.
The majority of the victims - 51 people - were shot dead, many in the head or chest, according to the report.
However, there has been little genuine accountability, said Anish Acharya, 19, who came with flowers to pay his respects.
"Why did we sacrifice our lives? What did we get? There is no hope that change will come. Oli was arrested the next day, but what then? The culprits are out and walking free," he told AFP.
"The government has not valued our sacrifices and demands," he said.
Shah's administration is facing its toughest challenge since taking power as it leads rescue and recovery efforts following cataclysmic glacial floods on the border with China.
The Aug 26 disaster killed at least 1,399 people in the two countries, including 1,356 in Nepal, according to official tolls.
A total of 5,500 people are still missing in Nepal and China.

7785ce3e9adbc597: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Negeri Sembilan has been thrust again into its unprecedented constitutional crisis, with claims that new Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim allegedly signed a proclamation to depose the state’s ruler, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, just one day after swearing an oath of allegiance to him.

According to The Straits Times, the explosive allegation was made public in a September 5 statement by the state’s four traditional ruling chieftains, the Undang Yang Empat, who possess customary authority under Adat Perpatih to elect and — they claim — dismiss the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.

When pressed on the allegations on September 6, Ismail did not directly deny signing the decree, stating only that “the four Undang have the right to their opinion” while reaffirming that he “and the state government express full loyalty to Muhriz Munawir as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar”.
The standoff is the most recent escalation yet in a months-long palace conflict that could colour Malaysian politics ahead of key elections.

According to the statement released by the four chieftains, Ismail met them on August 3 alongside throne contender Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar, the cousin of Tuanku Muhriz and son of the previous ruler.
The chieftains alleged that Ismail signed the formal proclamation ousting Tuanku Muhriz during this gathering, paving the way for Tuanku Nadzaruddin’s installation.

Sources told The Straits Times that the private meeting was attended by top Umno leaders, including party president and Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
All three reportedly declined requests for comment.

However, legal and government sources told The Straits Times that Ismail has privately claimed he was coerced into signing the document under severe political duress, alleging that Umno’s central leadership orchestrated the manoeuvre alongside the chieftains.
The same sources indicated that Ismail is preparing to lodge an official police report regarding the incident today.

Despite the purported signing on August 3, Ismail proceeded to swear in his state executive council before Tuanku Muhriz four days later on August 7, entrenching an extraordinary constitutional contradiction.
This development will again put the spotlight on Umno’s role in the Negeri Sembilan constitutional crisis.

Ahead of last month’s state election, Umno’s state lawmakers had withdrawn support for the menteri besar at the time, Datuk Seri Aminudin Harun, ostensibly for his public support of Tuanku Muhriz in the public row with the four Undang, before suddenly reversing this position.
Umno had sought to mitigate this prior to the election by positioning itself as a “mediator” to resolve the royal crisis.

“This is about crisis management. It’s how you manage the crisis. That is why the rakyat must consider all factors before they decide,” said Negeri Sembilan Umno chief Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias, one of the key personalities in the move to oust Aminudin

b604841ff1cd64e6: KUCHING: Persoalan sama ada 17 kerusi baharu DUN Sarawak sempat digunakan pada PRN akan datang masih sukar ditentukan.

Ahli Suruhanjaya Pilihan Raya (SPR) Mohd Faisal Syam Abdol Hazis berkata, keputusan itu bergantung kepada dua faktor, iaitu tempoh penyelesaian kajian semula persempadanan kerusi terlibat dan tarikh pembubaran DUN Sarawak.
Dua faktor ini, katanya, menyebabkan SPR belum dapat memberikan kepastian mengenai perkara itu.
“Pertama, kita perlu menyempurnakan kajian semula persempadanan ini sebelum 17 kerusi baharu ini dapat dikuatkuasakan. SPR diberi tempoh dua tahun untuk melengkapkan proses berkenaan.

“Yang kedua, kita tidak tahu bila DUN Sarawak akan dibubarkan. Yang kita tahu ialah DUN Sarawak akan bubar secara automatik pada Februari 2027,” katanya semasa menjadi tetamu program Influencer@Japen yang disiarkan melalui Facebook Japen Sarawak hari ini.
Pada 1 Sept lepas, SPR mula mempamerkan notis cadangan bagi menambah kawasan pilihan raya baharu dan pertukaran nama kawasan pilihan raya di Sarawak.
Notis berkenaan akan dipamerkan hingga 30 Sept di beberapa pejabat daerah di seluruh Sarawak bagi membolehkan orang ramai mengemukakan bantahan.

Menurut notis itu, SPR mengikut kehendak Fasal (2) Perkara 113 Perlembagaan Persekutuan telah mengkaji semula pembahagian negeri Sarawak kepada bahagian-bahagian pilihan raya persekutuan dan bahagian-bahagian PRN.
Hasil kajian itu sebanyak 17 kawasan pilihan raya negeri baharu telah dicadangkan, manakala 10 lagi dicadangkan untuk ditukar nama.
Selain itu, terdapat satu kawasan pilihan raya persekutuan dalam negeri Sarawak dicadangkan untuk ditukar nama.

Sementara itu, mengulas mengenai kajian semula persempadanan kerusi DUN Sarawak, Mohd Faisal Syam berkata, kajian itu perlu disiapkan dalam tempoh dua tahun selepas notis diwartakan pada 1 Sept lepas.
Katanya, terdapat beberapa peringkat atau proses yang perlu diselesaikan sebelum 17 kerusi baharu itu dapat dikuatkuasakan.
“Sekarang ini, kita berada pada proses pameran notis. Selepas pameran ini, jika ada bantahan, kita kena buat siasatan tempatan. Itu juga perlu mengambil masa.

“Selepas tempoh bantahan itu, SPR perlu duduk semula dan meneliti semua bantahan tersebut. Mana yang 'valid', kita terima dan kita tambah baik. Selepas itu kita ada pameran kali kedua untuk tempoh sebulan juga.
“Selepas semua selesai, kita akan serahkan laporan akhir kepada perdana menteri,” katanya.

d21e5183ae006278: KUALA LUMPUR: Dasar Ekonomi Baru (DEB) yang diperkenalkan pada 1971 bagi membasmi kemiskinan dan meningkatkan taraf hidup Bumiputera miskin, telah menyuburkan budaya kebergantungan serta terlalu memanjakan orang Melayu, kata seorang tokoh perbankan dan bekas timbalan perdana menteri.
Bekas Pengerusi Kumpulan CIMB, Nazir Razak, berkata DEB pada asalnya hanya dirancang untuk dilaksanakan selama 20 tahun.
Malah katanya, bekas timbalan perdana menteri Dr Ismail Abdul Rahman menyifatkannya sebagai satu bentuk langkah sementara selama 20 tahun.

"Kita akan menghadapi masalah serius jika ia diteruskan. Dan apabila ia berlanjutan terlalu lama, 'budaya tongkat' ini menjadi sebati," kata Nazir, yang juga anak kepada perdana menteri kedua Abdul Razak Hussein.

Beliau berkata demikian pada forum bertajuk 'Mengenang Tun Abdul Razak: Arkitek Pembangunan dan Pembinaan Negara Malaysia', ketika menjawab soalan sama ada DEB perlu diubah suai, digantikan atau dikaji semula.
Beliau berkata DEB perlu dikaji semula dengan memberi tumpuan lebih besar kepada pendidikan dan pembangunan profesional.

"DEB terlalu memberi tumpuan kepada pengagihan saham dan pemilikan. Dan apabila kita mengambil pendekatan itu, muncul segala macam 'Ali Baba'," katanya, merujuk kepada budaya mencari keuntungan melalui keistimewaan atau peluang yang diberikan tanpa persaingan sebenar.
"Saya fikir kita memberi tumpuan kepada tema yang salah dalam pelaksanaan DEB."
Nazir turut mengkritik pemberian kontrak kepada syarikat Bumiputera, sambil mempersoalkan mengapa ahli politik dibenarkan memilih penerima kontrak tersebut.
"Mereka (ahli politik) tidak mahu persaingan dalam kalangan Bumiputera," katanya, sambil menambah bahawa kekurangan persaingan telah melemahkan perniagaan Bumiputera.
Musa Hitam, yang berkhidmat sebagai timbalan perdana menteri dari 1981 hingga 1986, berkata dasar berkenaan secara tidak langsung telah mewujudkan budaya bergantung kepada bantuan kerajaan.
"Bagi saya, dasar ekonomi untuk orang Melayu telah menyebabkan orang Melayu menjadi terlalu dimanjakan. Dimanjakan oleh kerajaan," katanya.

Beliau berkata DEB bukan sahaja membantu orang Melayu, malah turut memberi manfaat kepada negara secara keseluruhannya. Bagaimanapun, katanya, dasar itu juga mewujudkan perasaan tidak yakin dalam kalangan masyarakat.
"Orang takut tidak mendapat apa-apa, tetapi walaupun mereka menerima bantuan, mereka mengatakan ia tidak mencukupi dan meminta lebih banyak lagi."

bea1216164bc5c98: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The Communications Ministry is prepared to work with the Home Ministry, the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, police and relevant agencies to strengthen e-commerce regulation and curb the sale of prohibited goods, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said such cooperation was important as there were still gaps in the country’s e-commerce ecosystem, particularly as e-commerce platforms are currently not subject to licensing.

“There are indeed gaps in the e-commerce system. At present, e-commerce is not yet licensed, so we need to look into this matter,” he told reporters on the sidelines of the Huawei WAIC Connect Malaysia 2026 Symposium today.

Fahmi said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) had held a meeting with a major platform yesterday, but he had yet to receive an update on the outcome of the meeting as of this morning.

He said most e-commerce platforms in Malaysia prohibit the sale of prohibited products, including drugs such as fentanyl, but expressed concern that one platform appeared to be too lax in allowing such products to be offered.
“The accounts selling these prohibited products may be fake accounts,” he said.

Fahmi stressed that platforms needed to address the issue of fake accounts being created and the sale of prohibited products, rather than merely removing search keywords, which could make such products harder to find without addressing the actual problem.
“That should not be the way,” he said, adding that platforms needed to prevent fake accounts from being created for the purpose of selling drugs.
Previously, MCMC was instructed to hold meetings with e-commerce platforms following concerns over the online sale of drugs, including fentanyl and a substance referred to as “piu-piu”.
Fahmi said he had received a message from Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim regarding the phenomenon, which was seen as increasingly worrying. — Bernama
1b07cf058dd4ff00: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Malaysians have voiced their desire for Malaysia to have a political financing law to regulate political parties’ funding before the 16th general election, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said today.
Azalina’s remarks were based on findings from the Prime Minister’s Department’s Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) public engagement sessions.

“I was informed by the BHEUU deputy director general (policy) many voices of the public wants, if possible, that this Act can be in force before the 16th general election,” she said at the Political Financing Convention 2026 held at the Asian International Arbitration Centre (AIAC) building.

Azalina said the views of political parties would have to be obtained before the proposed political financing law is brought to Parliament, as it would be politicians in Parliament who would vote on whether to introduce such a law.
“So they are the users and they will vote on the law. So you must have them to have more say. If not, the delay of the Act may happen if there is no buy-in from political parties,” she said.
Earlier in the same speech, Azalina said she understood the debates, criticism and public anxiety over the process to introduce a political financing law not being as quick as other reform agendas.
“And certainly the people have the right to hope for changes and to demand the government fulfill the commitment as soon as possible.

“But on behalf of the government, I admit that the agenda of institutional legal reform, when we talk about political financing, is not a process that is that simple and capable of being implemented so quickly,” she said, emphasising the need for political parties to be stakeholders and to give their views since the proposed law would apply to them.

“Political will is not just measured by how quickly a reform is presented, but it also has to be evaluated based on the courage to start it, the readiness to accept views and criticism, and the strength of determination to carry it out,” she added.

Earlier in the speech, Azalina said BHEUU had taken over studies on the proposed political financing law since May 2023, and that the Cabinet had on September 8, 2023 agreed in principle to the drafting of the law and decided on further studies on the policy scope.
Azalina noted that BHEUU had carried out engagement work on the proposed law reform over the past two years.

Later at a press conference, Azalina replied to a question on why the political financing law had yet to be introduced in Malaysia, saying this was due to studies being carried out over the past two years: “The delay is not a political delay, but delay in terms of process and procedure done by BHEUU.”
Asked if it was possible for the proposed political financing law to be introduced before GE16, Azalina said the question of when GE16 would be held should be directed to the prime minister.
As for the timeline for how soon the law could be introduced, Azalina said, “I wish it’s as soon as possible”, but that it would depend on the work being done to prepare the Bill.

At the press conference, Azalina outlined various technical aspects of the proposed political financing law that have to be considered before it is brought to the Cabinet, and also proposed that BHEUU collect the written official opinions of all registered political parties in Malaysia on whether they agree to such a law.
Findings show 90.3 per cent want political financing law before GE16

Earlier at the convention, BHEUU deputy director-general (policy and development) Datuk Punitha Silivarajoo presented the findings from BHEUU’s engagement involving 1,544 participants nationwide in 12 engagement sessions from June to November 2025.

Punitha said 100 per cent of the 1,544 participants agreed that Malaysia needs to have a political financing law, and that 90.3 per cent of the 1,544 wanted this law to be tabled and passed in Parliament before the next general election.

Out of the 1,544 participants, 67 per cent were political parties and grassroots leaders, 17 per cent were government agencies and academics, 11 per cent were non-governmental organisations (NGOs), civil society organisations (CSOs) and youths, and five per cent were from the business sector.
A total of 32 political parties and 69 NGOs and CSOs were consulted in the engagement sessions with 1,544 participants.
d1f20a7b04c120dc: KUALA LUMPUR: The New Economic Policy (NEP), introduced in 1971 to eradicate poverty and uplift poor Bumiputeras, cultivated a culture of dependency and mollycoddled the Malays, an ex-banker and a former deputy prime minister said today.
Former CIMB Group chairman Nazir Razak said the NEP was only meant to continue for 20 years.
He said former deputy prime minister Dr Ismail Abdul Rahman even labelled it a 20-year "handicap".

"We will be in serious trouble if we have to continue. And when it goes on for too long, this 'tongkat culture' becomes deeply embedded," Nazir, the son of second prime minister Abdul Razak Hussein, added.

He said this at a forum titled "Remembering Tun Abdul Razak: Architect of Malaysia's Development and Nation Building", responding to a question on whether the NEP should be remodelled, replaced or reviewed.
He said the NEP should be reviewed, with a pivot in focus towards education and professional development.
"The NEP focused too much on the distribution of shares and ownership. And when you go down that path, all these 'Ali Babas' come up," he said, using the phrase to refer to a culture of rent-seeking.
"I think we focused on the wrong theme in the execution of the NEP."
Nazir also criticised the awarding of contracts to Bumiputera businesses, asking why politicians were allowed to choose the recipients.
"They (politicians) don't want competition among Bumiputeras," he said, adding that the lack of competition had weakened Bumiputera businesses.
Musa Hitam, who served as deputy prime minister from 1981 to 1986, said the policy inadvertently produced a culture of reliance on government assistance.
"To me, the economic policy for the Malays has caused the Malays to become too pampered. Pampered by the government," he added.
He said the NEP had helped not only Malays but the country as a whole, adding however that it also created a sense of insecurity.
"People fear receiving nothing, but even when they receive assistance, they say it is not enough and ask for more."
dcb5f4b9a3dc5da4: KUALA LUMPUR: Timbalan Perdana Menteri Zahid Hamidi mencadangkan Indeks Mobiliti Pendidikan Melayu dibangunkan bagi mengukur sejauh mana pendidikan berjaya meningkatkan kedudukan sosioekonomi masyarakat Melayu.

Zahid berkata indeks itu perlu menjejaki perjalanan seseorang secara menyeluruh, bermula daripada latar sosioekonomi, pencapaian pembelajaran dan laluan pengajian hingga kepada pekerjaan, kesepadanan kemahiran dan perkembangan pendapatan.

Menurutnya, pendidikan tidak seharusnya dinilai hanya berdasarkan tempoh seseorang berada dalam sistem atau kelayakan yang diperoleh, sebaliknya perlu mengambil kira ilmu dan kemahiran yang dikuasai serta kesannya terhadap mobiliti sosial.
“Dalam teori modal insan, pendidikan ialah pelaburan. Tetapi pelaburan itu hanya benar-benar menjadi modal apabila ia menghasilkan keupayaan dan mobiliti yang nyata.

“Sebab itu ukuran kita mesti bergerak daripada schooling kepada learning, dan daripada learning kepada mobiliti – bukan hanya berapa lama seseorang berada dalam sistem, tetapi apa yang dikuasainya, ke mana ilmu itu membawanya dan sejauh mana pendidikan meningkatkan mobiliti sosialnya,” katanya.
Zahid yang juga presiden Umno berkata demikian ketika berucap pada Konvensyen Pendidikan Melayu bertajuk AUKU dan Hala Tuju Pendidikan Tinggi Negara di Pusat Dagangan Dunia (WTC) Kuala Lumpur.
Beliau berkata Sekretariat Pendidikan dan Penyelidikan Umno bersama institusi akademik perlu membangunkan kerangka awal indeks berkenaan sebelum diteliti dan dibawa ke peringkat dasar.
Menurutnya, tugas itu akan dilaksanakan Pengerusi Konvensyen Pendidikan Melayu 2026 Zambry Abd Kadir bersama timbalannya, Idris Jusoh.
Zahid berkata agenda pendidikan Melayu selepas ini perlu lebih berasaskan data, hasil dan bukti, bukan sekadar diukur melalui jumlah program, peruntukan atau peserta.

Katanya, selama beberapa dekad tumpuan utama pendidikan Melayu adalah memperluas akses menerusi pembinaan sekolah serta penubuhan dan pengembangan institusi seperti MARA, MRSM dan UiTM, selain penyediaan biasiswa serta peluang ke pendidikan tinggi.

Namun, katanya, cabaran kini bukan lagi sekadar memastikan orang Melayu mendapat tempat dalam sistem pendidikan, tetapi memastikan mereka keluar dengan ilmu dan kemahiran yang bernilai serta berupaya meningkatkan kedudukan diri dan keluarga.

Beliau berkata pendidikan juga perlu diterjemahkan kepada nilai ekonomi, terutama apabila 35.2% pekerja berpendidikan tertiari pada suku kedua tahun ini masih bekerja dalam pekerjaan yang tidak sepadan dengan tahap kemahiran mereka.

Zahid berkata walaupun Rancangan Malaysia Ke-13 (RMK13) menyasarkan kadar graduan yang bekerja setara dengan kelayakan meningkat daripada 69.4% kepada 70.1% menjelang 2030, institusi yang mempunyai mandat besar terhadap Bumiputera perlu meletakkan sasaran lebih tinggi.
Beliau mahu institusi berkenaan menyasarkan sekurang-kurangnya 80% graduan memperoleh pekerjaan yang sepadan dengan kelayakan mereka.

Terdahulu, konvensyen itu meluluskan tujuh resolusi untuk dibawa ke Kabinet, termasuk cadangan membangunkan pangkalan data dan indeks mobiliti pendidikan nasional, melaksanakan intervensi awal pendidikan secara bersasar serta memanfaatkan alumni UiTM untuk kembali menyumbang.

287423c7e888fdae: SEMPORNA: Kerajaan Sabah membelanjakan lebih RM1 bilion ketika ini bagi menangani masalah bekalan air di negeri itu.
Ketua Menteri, Hajiji Noor, berkata peruntukan itu antaranya bagi menggantikan paip usang di kebanyakan daerah, termasuk dicuri.

"Di samping itu, satu daripada projek (air) yang besar ini akan siap pada hujung tahun ini dan perkembangan projek di Tawau lebih kurang 50% ke 60%," katanya selepa menyempurnakan pelancaran 106 unit kedai dua tingkat Fasa 1 serta pecah tanah projek komersial fasa 2 dan 3 Lembaga Pembangunan Perumahan dan Bandar (LPPB) di Jalan Bubul di sini.
Beliau berkata, kerajaannya berusaha mengatasi isu kemudahan asas air, elektrik dan jalan raya yang dihadapi rakyat sejak sekian lama.
Sementara itu, Hajiji berkata, kerajaan negeri di bawah kepimpinannya mempunyai dasar mesra pelabur bagi memastikan ekonomi Sabah terus maju.

"Kita gubal satu dasar yang memudahkan pemaju dan juga pelabur dari luar datang ke Sabah kerana jika ada pelaburan, aktiviti ekonomi akan lancar dan peluang pekerjaan untuk rakyat dapat diwujudkan, itu kita galakkan."
Jelasnya, pembangunan Sabah bukan tanggungjawab kerajaan semata-mata, sebaliknya memerlukan kerjasama semua pihak, termasuk sektor swasta, agensi pelaksana, usahawan dan rakyat.
Terdahulu, Hajiji dalam ucapannya berkata, pembangunan Sabah tidak patut hanya dilihat pada Kota Kinabalu atau bandar besar, tetapi setiap daerah.
Mengenai pelancaran projek LPPB hari ini, katanya, perkara itu perlu dilihat sebagai sebahagian perjalanan pembangunan Sabah, bukannya hanya satu projek komersial.

"Semporna mempunyai aset semula jadi sangat bernilai, iaitu keindahan pulau, namun untuk memastikan potensi tersebut dapat diterjemahkan kepada manfaat ekonomi lebih besar kepada rakyat, kita memerlukan pembangunan saling melengkapi."

Beliau berkata, kedudukan strategik kawasan komersial Jalan Bubul di sepanjang laluan utama Balung-Semporna memberi potensi untuk kawasan itu berkembang sebagai antara kawasan perdagangan dan perniagaan baharu.
Katanya, kawasan pembangunan itu juga mempunyai kelebihan kerana terdapat sungai dan berhampiran dengan laut, serta sesuai untuk pertimbangan pemaju membina sebuah jeti.
Hajiji berkata, jeti yang sesuai dan cantik mampu memberi nilai tambah, manakala orang ramai dapat menikmati pemandangan sungai dan laut, bersantai, menikmati matahari terbenam serta bergambar.
d773ecaeed1ce209: SEMPORNA: The Sabah government has spent over RM1 billion to address water supply-related problems in the state, chief minister Hajiji Noor says.
He said this included replacing ageing water pipes in most districts, and those that had been stolen.
"In addition, one of the two or three major (water) projects will be ready by the end of this year, while the project in Tawau is about 50% to 60% complete," he said here today.
He said the government is also working to address long-standing issues related to basic water, electricity and road facilities.
On investments, he said the state government has an open policy to ensure that Sabah continues to progress, including the economic front.

"We have formulated a policy to facilitate developers and foreign investors coming to Sabah because when there is investment, economic activities will run smoothly and employment opportunities can be created for the people.
"This is something we encourage," he said.

He added that development in Sabah was not solely the government’s responsibility, but required cooperation from all parties, including the private sector, implementation agencies, entrepreneurs and the people.
380feca1dc2b014b: SEPANG: Pakatan Harapan (PH) giat mempersiapkan jentera untuk menghadapi pelbagai senario pada PRN Melaka termasuk kemungkinan bertanding tanpa kerjasama dengan gabungan lain.
Pengarah Pilihan Raya PH, Amirudin Shari berkata setakat ini belum ada rundingan rasmi mengenai kerjasama antara PH dengan Barisan Nasional (BN) diadakan bagi menghadapi PRN berkenaan.

4b9f9c6818700f2b: Australia’s government will introduce legislation that tries to regulate digital services and impose a “digital duty of care.” “For too long, tech companies have been running real-time, unregulated product testing on Australians,” Minister for Communications Anika Wells said today. “In the same way that we have safety standards for cars, for food, and for appliances, Australia is getting basic safety standards for the online tools and online services,” she added. “Tech companies will still be allowed to move fast, but they will not be able to break things.” Meta, in its early years when still known as Facebook, used the term “Move fast and break things” to describe its internal processes for creating and updating its services. The premise of Australia’s plans is that Meta, and other digital platforms, broke far more than they intended in pursuit of profit. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese framed the planned digital duty of care as a successor to the law that means social media companies are not allowed to provide accounts to children aged under 16. “We would no longer let Australian children be treated as commodities,” he said. “We have the opportunity to shape tech for the better, rather than have it shape us.” The proposed law aims to shape tech by requiring social media companies to give Australian users the chance to determine what they see in their feeds. Some in Australia have criticized the planned law as government censorship. Albanese tried to counter that notion by summarizing the intent of the plan as “My feed, my way.” “This is not about giving government control,” Albanese said. “It is about giving people control.” Wells explained those controls would be implemented with a requirement for digital platforms of offer Australian users the chance to opt into a user experience that only shows content from accounts they already follow online. She said users will be able to opt back into an algorithmic feed and change their minds about what they want to see as often as they like. However, the law will also mean the relevant minister can seek a vote to ban certain content. Albanese said the draft bill seeks to do that for content that glorifies crime, promotes terrorism, pertains to eating disorders, pornography, sexual violence, and misogyny. Wells explained that the process of declaring content harmful would start with the relevant minister consulting with Australia’s e-Safety Commissioner, who will be able to recommend that certain types of content be declared harmful. That recommendation would be subject to a parliamentary vote before coming into force. Finding precedents in a bottle The use of the term “digital duty of care” is a reference to one of the foundational cases in the law of torts – 1932’s Donoghue v Stevenson, which concerns a woman who poured a bottle of ginger beer over ice cream and watched in horror as a decomposed snail slid into her snack. Donoghue later suffered a bout of gastro-enteritis. The landmark case found that the maker of the ginger beer – and any other provider of goods and services – has a responsibility to avoid any foreseeable harms caused by their acts or omissions. The case made the concept of a duty of care central to the law of torts, which cover civil harms. Australia naming its digital regulations a “digital duty of care” therefore puts the proposal firmly in the heart of western legal tradition. At the press conference announcing the planned legislation, Albanese and Wells called on parents whose children took their own lives after using social media, and advocates for tighter regulation of social media – all of whom were unsurprisingly in favor of the law and praised the government for having the courage to advance it. When discussing Australia’s social media ban, Albanese nearly always admits it is not perfect and would not mean all Australian children under 16 immediately vanish from social media. “We knew it would not be perfect but would not let that be the enemy of the good,” he said today, and then said Australia’s policy “Started a global movement” that has since seen over 20 countries impose social media bans for children. The PM suggested a digital duty of care could catch on, too, and Wells agreed. “There is a global reckoning coming for big tech,” she said. “And it started in Australia.” ®
